This is one of those old-school RPG's that are unforgiving. When you die, you don't even get a game over screen. You just continue watching the enemy walking over your corpse and doing... whatever it is that they do while waiting to fight with the hero, until you load the game and try again. As absurd it sounds, it sums up this game's difficulty and unforgiving attitude perfectly.
Clunky controls contribute to the amount of deaths and they do take a bit time to get used to, especially if you're running away (you'll be doing it quite a bit) in tight corridors. Also navigating the menus is a hassle, your items are all messed up, there is only one big slot in every category where everything is :D It literally is a big mess.
Thankfully the HUD has quick buttons for potions, skills and gear so you don't need to rely much on the inventory screen, and you can assign your own on the function keys (F1 - F9).
We have 3 classes, the classics: Warrior, Mage and a roque, female and male versions, only thing they determine is the unique skill and which stat starts at a higher level. Otherwise you can build your character how you see fit. All the skills from all 3 classes are available. 4 primary stats being Strength, Agility, Intelligence and Constitution, you can make a wizard with a body like a barbarian, if you must. Options for different builds are plenty, each class has usefull skills for everyone, but concentrating only on one class is a totally viable strategy as well.
The world itself is large, dungeons (and the world) are filled with secrets, skeletons, orcs and dwarves, NPC's have lot to say and you can pretty much choose your own path to walk. You can act rude towards everyone and suffer the consequences, unlike many other rpg's, dialoque choices do matter, they can make your life easy, hard or even get you killed if you bother the wrong person. Dialoque itself is interesting and a pleasure to read, there are funny sayings here and there, or general randomness that's happening in peoples lives.
YES! If you can get past the oldish/clunky controls and aren't afraid of a hard game, this is a solid one! Lots of funny things, exploring and finding, unforgiving but rewarding. Steam overlay or windowed mode isn't supported sadly, but no other annoyances or bugs encountered as of yet!

To me, at least, it's a little bit like building a giant ant farm - give it all the resources it needs to survive, and then watch the prison go through its routine, changing some things around every now and then. There are fewer rules and challenges compared to something like Rimworld but the tradeoff is more creativity and more freedom.

I finished this game twice in order to try the max difficulty: FUBAR, which you unlock after completing the game once. The game still look awesome in 2017, I really enjoyed the desert/appocalyptic landscape of Dubai. The story, even though it's perfect gives you some choices and has a big moral impact on the three main characters: Cpt. The campaign lenght is very reasonable (around 8-12 hours if you play on high difficulty and collect all Intel) and I like how the chapter's succeed like a journey (chapter's menu is done really nice). The soundtrack is very good and contributes a lot to the atmosphere. Even though the game doesn't try to recreate Dubai architecture exactly, the level design is done nicely and it's quite diverse. The AI does it's job, but it's not very smart (doesn't change location often enough, his head pops out of cover, your teamates often go in the middle of the enemies which is not realistic etc.), the onkly advantage is the 1-2 shot kill on Fubar, which makes you play the game more slowly, moving from cover to cover. The thing that annoyed me the most are some level design locations/missions that rely a lot on luck than skill and if you are unlucky (like me) you end up spending 1h in a location that should take you 5 min max to complete. Anyway this remains a great game with a good story and a reasonable price.

*Got in the Humble Monthly, I have played this quite a lot before before release via the original demo and closed test*
What is MorphBlade?
Morphblade is a very simple puzzle game where you are initially thrown into a game without any knowledge of how to play and you have to figure it out, it's very simple to get the hang of and each game is randomly generated, there is no story or levels you just play until you die and restart into a brand new randomly generated level. There are a few different enemies that will cause problems and you will have to figure out a strategy to beat them.
-GamePlay-
Essentially each game you have to defeat every enemy and after that you choose a hex with a powerup that you want on and then the next wave begins, there are different upgrades you can get by defeating enemies on different hex's. I don't want to go into too much detail on how to play the game as it's best to figure that out on your own though it is very easy to get the hang of.
-Worth £4?-
To be honest it very much depends on whether you like repeating the same things over and over again without any "Goal", it's a very fun puzzle game which I'll definitely turn on every now and then and have a quick few games though I would love to see this as a mobile game. So if you can ignore the lack of "Goal" then Yes, if not then I'd say no.
-Conclusion-
A very fun but short puzzle game with random levels. I give it a 7.5/10 Just because it lacks content, such as an end goal (Campaign, Scenarios etc) which could have added more to it without feeling somewhat empty.

Small Spoiler Alert
For one who is new to the DmC series, this game was fairly entertaining in gameplay and story. Storywise the plot was simple, Dante and his allies have an enemy they must kill, in order to do so you have to go through many levels, taking down the enemies along the way while completing different tasks all resolved through battle. Easy to follow and understand.
Dialogue is average, it isn't too bad, but it doesn't stand out either. Nothing fancy and not too memorable, but dialogue is not the game's forte.
Gameplay was where it stands out as it's smooth and incredibly easy to understand and use when compared to the previous games as I have seen. The player is given many different weapons as they progress through the levels and complete them and are able to upgrade them, by using these weapons to their fullest the player can amass amazing and long combos much more easily than the previous DmC games making it easier to be more invovled and more focused, increasing the game's value. Gameplay definitely helps in the overall value
The characters, Dante is a somewhat foul mouthed individual, young and rebellious to society and authorities from how he acts, not caring much for others except who he's invovled with.
His brother and ally Vergil is calm and intelligent, different from the rash and reckless Dante, Vergil makes the plans behinds the scenes and is the leader of the terriorist organisation that are trying to awaken the world to the terror of Demons through media as well as fighting them, mainly fighting them by deploying Dante.
Kat, the third character, part of Virgil's organisation and finds Dante, during the game Dante forms a bond with her, reaching the point where both share private information about each other delving into their backstory and how they came to be who they are.
The problems or little quiks I have is that firstly, the devil trigger didnt' really feel anywhere near as powerful as hoped, it would launch enemies into the air, leaving them defenseless in the air and encourages you to perform air combos, but this constricts your combos as you are forced to do them in the air. For players that are used to action games they may find this easier to adapt to then newer players.
My second problem with the devil trigger is the physical changes to Dante when used, all that happens is his hair changes to white, his eyes are red and his coat changes to red, I have seen the previous design of Dante and I find this to be a bit lazy.
Also the devil trigger, while I may find it's physical changes lazy I've looked up the devil trigger from the previous games and when compared, it could've been much better, at the least they could have given us some type of amazing armour like the previous games. Transformations like the devil trigger are meant to make the one playing feel powerful, not invincible, but just incredibly powerful, a drastic change in appearance like armour would have helped achieved that. But with the devil trigger as it is, I completely forgot I had it for the majority of the game and barely used it, but didn't affect the game much, I just would've liked something more, would've made the Devil Trigger more memorable and something to look forward to during gameplay.
Next problem is with one of the weapons, primarily Ebony and Ivory, your first pair of guns, when using them they felt extremely weak compared to all the other weapons, I know the player is encouraged to chain combos together to maximise their score, but Ebony and Ivory in general were the weapons I used the least. They don't make the enemy flinch or cause much damage, I didn't find much reason to use them, they just could've been better.
Next will be the positive aspects of this game, weapons, you get a large variety and you can chain them together however you like, whether you want to use firearms and switch straight to the rebellion or the other weapons giving you a large variety of combos you can pull off as previously mentioned in the gameplay section and during gameplay you'll develop a favourite.
The missions, they're well done, visually appeasing to the eyes and are a bit linear, but this is a hack and slash game, so level exploration is limited but still exists, by exploring the level you may find bonuses that add to your score such as lost souls, items to help you in battle or otherwise or keys to open the doors to secret missions. These secret missions vary some being harder than others but all the ones I have come across challenge your skills in the game by placing restrictions on how you go about killing your enemies or what you do. These missions are fun and optional for those who want to get a little bit more out of the game.
Next is that levels are separated into sections or missions, for example Mission 1, Mission 2, by separating them the player may venture back into previous missions in order to find a collectible, secret mission or improve your score if you so wish.
Platforming in the levels is easy enough, not too easy and not too hard as long as you're paying attention
Next on the agenda is the scoring system during combat, by amassing combos and avoiding damage a player can easily build up their score and the multiplier known as style ranks which rates how well you do during combat and how well you did during the mission.
The higher your style rank the higher your score, simple, but whether or not this counts as a positive depends on the player, for players that aren't good at action and fighting games they will find this to be a positive experience as well as those who enjoy a high score based on performance, however for the more hardcore players or more expectant ones, once the style rank has reached a rank it will not go below that rank unless the player gets hit, for this the difficulty in which to receive a high score may be too easy for those hardcore players.
However fear not, for those who love extremely difficult enemies there are higher difficulty levels, seven in all, the first three are available from the beginning and to unlock the harder ones you have to play on the hardest difficulty possible with the exception of Son of Sparda. So enjoy.
Overral it is enjoyable, new players can get into the groove of battle quickly and easily while learning how to use the weapons while finding that the story isn't complicated and easy to follow, levels can be explored to find little collectibles and challenges. Levels can be repeated numerous times for max efficiency and the highest score as many times as you would like. Characters are likeable, you won't fall in love with them, but you do begin to like them. Devil Trigger, Ebony and Ivory and the style ranking could be changed or adjusted during gameplay based on individual preferences.
But other than that the game is enjoyable, not perfect, but still a good game. However the replay value isn't high, for most people one playthrough is more than enough.

This is one of the most well-known Half-Life 2 (and Half-Life in general) mods and for good reason. The mod does start off with the player getting pretty much instantly attacked by combine soldiers. After this start and a mad dash around the tiny surface of the island, the player travels down below into a secret combine facility while an AI program communicates with them via text. I honestly wasn't able to pay enough attention to this text in the midst of the gameplay but the little that I did notice made for a pretty decent story, for a mod. As for the map design and gameplay, they really make these few extra levels so good. They feel almost like something out of an official Half-Life game. The pacing of enemies is also quite good. On the way down, when the facility is still intact, most (,if not, all) of the enemies are combine soldiers while on the way back up, loads of zombies start appearing as the player's surroundings crumble. These zombies are for the most part zombines which fits how the station's residents are all combine soldiers instead of the average-citizen zombies in City 17. The pacing is just so good and all of it is packed into one, pretty short, little mod. The weapon distribution is a little fast at the start, though it fits to that feeling of having an instant rush which, unlike in Half-Life Before, feels very fitting instead of sloppy. Just great on so many levels.

As a huge fan of "Original Sin", I wanted to experience this series' roots. If you have tolerance for old school gaming, and enjoy the newer Divinity games, and can
you can find some fun here. There the imp ZixZax, and the leveling system you love, and a zombie named Jake, and a healing stone that you can give to a mortally wounded solder (or hoard for yourself), and you can throw items all over the place and look for hidden keys and levers, and there's all those fun skills that feel like true stepping stones when you first obtain them.
The first area is a multilevel catacombs with puzzles and a few interesting and goofy characters and I'm thinking I can overlook the diablo-esqe combat system involving (mostly) clicking on a unit until they die. But then the baloney starts. There's these champions who will kill you in a couple hits, and unless you want to try to run past them, you are going to have to tough it out.  I finally got past the first few by kiting around them for 5 minutes and chipping away at their health with a little bow and arrow. Then, the next level down, there's like 10 more champions in a single area. Huh?
I finally "solved" it by powergaming and abusing skill systems. Ah-ha! The scorpion traps that the thief class has are absolutely gamebreaking. They can clear out a map solo with a little help. Cool! Powergaming in Divinity games is always my favorite part, and I was amused to see that in the 1st game, it was not merely optional as it was
.
So I solve that part, and I learn a bunch more skills, I get my teleport pyramids set up so I can warp back to a bedroom and heal up in a snap. I start doing sidequests. And there's still a lot of grinding, more than I'm comfortable with, but it's bearable and I was looking forward to each new level-up to see what I could do.
I make it about halfway into the game - I think - because there's still parts of the map that are inexplicably tough, but then my teleporter pyramids are taken away for story reasons, and I have to fight my way out of a crypt. The story is interesting leading up to this, but apparently I triggered this quest way too early because I'm about 15 levels too far behind and even my tricks don't save me now. It takes me six hours of kiting enemies to make it out alive and get back on the road. But my teleporter pyramids aren't returned yet. I check a guide and I've got to get about 10 hours down the main questline before I get them back.
That means grinding my character a LOT more, and now I have to do it without the benefit of fast travel back to town for a quick heal. No way. Not going to happen.  This is where I signed off.
I don't regret my time spent with "Divine Divinity" but I won't be finishing it, and I'd only suggest playing it if you want to see where it all began. Or, even better, do it with a walkthrough guidiing your course, and don't make the same unrecoverable mistakes I made.

Alright this is gonna be a long review.So let's get started!!!
This game its one of my all time favourites and for a good reason so I decided to make a review
Treyarch really nailded this tittle and its overall a really solid game and exeperience
PROS:
-A very good story and probably one of the best I've seen in quite some time
-Alex Mason and Frank Woods return from the first BO1 (I am so glad to see that BO2 is continuing the story of the first one unlike BO3 which not only had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ story and it had nothing to do with the first two games)
-David Mason,Mike Harper are also good characters (its nice to see that Alex has a son which is as badass as him)
-The game has multiple endings.Its something that the fans asked for a long time and its good to see that Treyarch and Activision listen to the community
-You can actually save Alex Mason in the mission ''Suffer With Me'' if you shoot him in the leg and at the end of the game he will come to The Vault to meet up with Woods and David (its so satisfying to see Alex reunited with his best friend and with his son)
-Very good level design and good mission structure
-You can costoumize your loadout before every mission
-Half of the game takes place in the 1980s and the other half in 2025.All together a good mix between old school and new school
-Good graphics for its time.I remember back in 2012 when I first played the game it looked realistic af even for CoD game
-The all time favourite Nuketown is back this time as Nuketown 2025.The new Nuketown feels exactly as fast-paced as the first one.Overall an amazing remake.Ah back when they knew how to remake maps.Other good examples are Uplink (Summit remake from BO1) and Studio (Firing Range remake from BO1)
-Large variety of weapons.From the classic M1911 and M16A1 to the modern SCAR-H and LSAT  There is something out there for everybody.Plus something that made me very happy the Balistic Knife and Crossbow from BO1 make a return and with a new modernized look to fit the tone of the game but they still feel as good as in the first game which is always a plus in my book
-Amazing and andrenaline pumping multiplayer with a few new game mods.The classic Wager Matches from the first game also make a return this time called Party Games.God knows how many hours I spent playing One In The Chamber,Sticks and Stones or Gun Game in BO1.Its hartwarming seeing them in BO2
-Raul Menendez is one the best antagonists of this generation.The writers really did an amazing job with this guy.The man is almost as good as Vaas from Far Cry 3 and that says a lot about how good this game is.
-The Zombies are amazing as well.My favourite definitely are Mob of The Dead (such a shame its a DLC) and Nuketown Zombies (the best map in multiplayer with zombies.What could you want more ?.And that giant mushroom cloud in the backround is stunning)
-CONS
-A game that came out 5 years ago still costs 59 euros ??? WTF Activision!!!. Just buy the game from a store its probably only 10 euros there.
-The players just destroy the multiplayer.You can only find matches of TDM and Nukejacked.And if you decide to play Nukejacked almost 99% of the time it will be only Nuketown and its a rarity if you ever catch Hijacked.Don't get me wrong Nuketown is an amazing map but pretty soon you will get tired of it because you will get wallbanged from across the map and spawntrapped A LOT.And you will die a lot because its ALWAYS HARDCORE.Such a shame we have so many toxic players in this games.This never happened in BO1.
Final thoughts:
A true masterpiece of a game.I think about I realize that THIS is last good CoD we had.And also this is the only good futuristic CoD we had.With NO EXOJUMPS,NO WEAPON VARIANTS AND NO SUPPLY DROPS.
BTW why is BO3 called BO3 ??? It has nothing to do with the first two games.So why its called BO3 ???.I will tell you why.Because brand recognition so Activision could make more money.Sorry if this was a long review.

It's not often I find myself saying, "I don't want to do this" in a video game but damnit if Spec Ops: The Line didn't make me say it more times than I can count. This game isn't afraid to give you an unflinching, uncompromising look into the madness of 3 soldiers whose worlds come crashing down around them when they are forced to commit some terrible acts in the name of survival and "The American Way". Call of Duty MW2 may have made a big splash with its' "No Russian" level years ago, but the NUMEROUS atrocities you take part in/witness within Spec Ops: The Line's at times disturbing narrative makes that level look like child's play. Without spoiling much more the best thing I can tell you to do is this:
Enjoy Lugo's jokes in the beginning while you can. It'll be the last time you'll smile while playing this game.

First of all, this was an absolutely fantastic game. I highly recommend it to anyone that enjoys a great story. It's dark, it's gritty, and it'll leave you feeling ashamed and guilty for the actions you take in the game. By the end I was blown away by just how deep and profound the story really was and in my opinion, it's games likew this that really drive home the argument that video games can be an art form.
Now on the flip side (and I have to adress this) the gameplay was very lackluster. It's little more than a generis over the shoulder third person shooter. The gun play felt weak and boring, the cover system was awful, the controls were wonky, clunky, and frustrsting. It left me feeling like the game was harder than it actually was.
Considering just how great the story was, it was more than worth the frustrating controls and the lackluster gameplay. I will probably come back and play this again at some point. Hard to give this a rating.

For one who is new to the DmC series, this game was fairly entertaining in gameplay and story. Storywise the plot was simple, Dante and his allies have an enemy they must kill, in order to do so you have to go through many levels, taking down the enemies along the way while completing different tasks all resolved through battle. Easy to follow and understand.
Dialogue is average, it isn't too bad, but it doesn't stand out either. Nothing fancy and not too memorable, but dialogue is not the game's forte.
Gameplay was where it stands out as it's smooth and incredibly easy to understand and use when compared to the previous games as I have seen. The player is given many different weapons as they progress through the levels and complete them and are able to upgrade them, by using these weapons to their fullest the player can amass amazing and long combos much more easily than the previous DmC games making it easier to be more invovled and more focused, increasing the game's value. Gameplay definitely helps in the overall value
The characters, Dante is a somewhat foul mouthed individual, young and rebellious to society and authorities from how he acts, not caring much for others except who he's invovled with.
His brother and ally Vergil is calm and intelligent, different from the rash and reckless Dante, Vergil makes the plans behinds the scenes and is the leader of the terriorist organisation that are trying to awaken the world to the terror of Demons through media as well as fighting them, mainly fighting them by deploying Dante.
Kat, the third character, part of Virgil's organisation and finds Dante, during the game Dante forms a bond with her, reaching the point where both share private information about each other delving into their backstory and how they came to be who they are.
The problems or little quiks I have is that firstly, the devil trigger didnt' really feel anywhere near as powerful as hoped, it would launch enemies into the air, leaving them defenseless in the air and encourages you to perform air combos, but this constricts your combos as you are forced to do them in the air. For players that are used to action games they may find this easier to adapt to then newer players.
My second problem with the devil trigger is the physical changes to Dante when used, all that happens is his hair changes to white, his eyes are red and his coat changes to red, I have seen the previous design of Dante and I find this to be a bit lazy.
Also the devil trigger, while I may find it's physical changes lazy I've looked up the devil trigger from the previous games and when compared, it could've been much better, at the least they could have given us some type of amazing armour like the previous games. Transformations like the devil trigger are meant to make the one playing feel powerful, not invincible, but just incredibly powerful, a drastic change in appearance like armour would have helped achieved that. But with the devil trigger as it is, I completely forgot I had it for the majority of the game and barely used it, but didn't affect the game much, I just would've liked something more, would've made the Devil Trigger more memorable and something to look forward to during gameplay.
Next problem is with one of the weapons, primarily Ebony and Ivory, your first pair of guns, when using them they felt extremely weak compared to all the other weapons, I know the player is encouraged to chain combos together to maximise their score, but Ebony and Ivory in general were the weapons I used the least. They don't make the enemy flinch or cause much damage, I didn't find much reason to use them, they just could've been better.
Next will be the positive aspects of this game, weapons, you get a large variety and you can chain them together however you like, whether you want to use firearms and switch straight to the rebellion or the other weapons giving you a large variety of combos you can pull off as previously mentioned in the gameplay section and during gameplay you'll develop a favourite.
The missions, they're well done, visually appeasing to the eyes and are a bit linear, but this is a hack and slash game, so level exploration is limited but still exists, by exploring the level you may find bonuses that add to your score such as lost souls, items to help you in battle or otherwise or keys to open the doors to secret missions. These secret missions vary some being harder than others but all the ones I have come across challenge your skills in the game by placing restrictions on how you go about killing your enemies or what you do. These missions are fun and optional for those who want to get a little bit more out of the game.
Next is that levels are separated into sections or missions, for example Mission 1, Mission 2, by separating them the player may venture back into previous missions in order to find a collectible, secret mission or improve your score if you so wish.
Platforming in the levels is easy enough, not too easy and not too hard as long as you're paying attention
Next on the agenda is the scoring system during combat, by amassing combos and avoiding damage a player can easily build up their score and the multiplier known as style ranks which rates how well you do during combat and how well you did during the mission.
The higher your style rank the higher your score, simple, but whether or not this counts as a positive depends on the player, for players that aren't good at action and fighting games they will find this to be a positive experience as well as those who enjoy a high score based on performance, however for the more hardcore players or more expectant ones, once the style rank has reached a rank it will not go below that rank unless the player gets hit, for this the difficulty in which to receive a high score may be too easy for those hardcore players.
However fear not, for those who love extremely difficult enemies there are higher difficulty levels, seven in all, the first three are available from the beginning and to unlock the harder ones you have to play on the hardest difficulty possible with the exception of Son of Sparda. So enjoy.
Overral it is enjoyable, new players can get into the groove of battle quickly and easily while learning how to use the weapons while finding that the story isn't complicated and easy to follow, levels can be explored to find little collectibles and challenges. Levels can be repeated numerous times for max efficiency and the highest score as many times as you would like. Characters are likeable, you won't fall in love with them, but you do begin to like them. Devil Trigger, Ebony and Ivory and the style ranking could be changed or adjusted during gameplay based on individual preferences.
But other than that the game is enjoyable, not perfect, but still a good game. However the replay value isn't high, for most people one playthrough is more than enough.

It's decent to good. Didn't live up to the hype for me at least, but I can see the appeal. Personally not a huge fan of the blue and lifeless metallic bases of the Combine, the ending of Half-Life 2 for me worked in spite of the aesthetic because of the story and overpowered gravity gun. It throws a lot of science mumbo jumbo at you through the text messages sent to you by a spooky commander type figure, expecting you to understand what all of it means. I eventually made it through the ''puzzles'', but expect a lot of running about pressing E to trigger things. Protip: every solution is either a button, or throwing a grenade into something, or turning valves. Pretty sure that covers most of the puzzles.
Very action packed, so that's good. Not that the level design is always made for combat, straight catwalks and huge open areas with little cover don't always facilitate gunplay. This is why -- while the map is complex in its design and though I don't understand some of the sci-fi it seems to make sense -- I don't consider this an absolute triumph of map design like some do because the gunfights can be poor depending on what area of the map you are on. It's definitely a technical achievement, since the mod doesn't have any typical loading screens.
Also, play this on normal. I tried Hard for a little while and got rekt very quickly, that difficulty is not designed for this mod.

If I had bought this at the launch, I'd probably not be charitable, but buying late on sale, I found it to be a great game.  For a full 60 dollar game, you only get six missions, some variants,  and a prologue, but if you catch it at a cheaper price, its definately worth it.  Each level is large and fairly open, and it takes its formatting from earlier games rather than taking Absolution as its launching point.  The mastery system gives you some good replay value simply for unlocking new items, and the professional difficulty gives you a chance to play the same levels over with a far stricter difficulty, introducing new challenges.  The levels themselves each feel different and are all very good, featuring both an into and an outro story segment that is quite interesting and builds up to the promise of a follow up.
There had been rumors of a season 2 in development, I don't know what it will be like, but its entirely possible the dev team will take as much care as they have for the first season of the new game and add in more quality content.  Hopefully it will be a reduced price, however, as the content simply isn't enough for a full-priced game.

HOLY CRAP!! What can I say about this game?! This is an amazing game and scratched an itch I didnt know I had? Lets do the generic pros and cons.
Pros:
-Polished, like really REALLY polished. Its the least buggy EA game iv played in a long time.
-Awesome controls. The way you pick up, load, and interact is awesome and feels right. This is how other games should play.
-Sense of exploration. You need minerals in order to progress. In order to find the minerals you need to do some cave diving or scower the planet surface for crashed space machines im which to salvage.
-Vehicles and planet jumping. Need I say more? The vehicles are slightly buggy (which is in cons) but most definetly playable. Getting to the point of exploring other planets pretty much blew my mind. You need to take into account other planet orbits. The planet you want to go to might not come into orbit unless YOU orbit another planet. Its the little things like this that I wish many other games had.
-Co-op. Also buggy (currently) but works. If you are like me, co-op is a big decider in game purchases and this game delivers.
-Lots of content. For being early access this game has tons of content. Tons of stuff to craft and many things to explore.
Now to Cons!
-Buggy. OBVIOUSLY. Its early access, Its meant for player feedback in order to improve. Vehicles seem a little unpredictable at times but its nothing game braking. I found myself getting stuck in the terrain rarely.
-Multiplayer(co-op) needs work, but the devs know this. Should be easier to play with a friend instead of steam overlay.
-Menu and options. The menu is bare bones. At the time of me writing this review they currently dont have a way to exit the game from the main menu? Maybe its me but I ended up just alt+tabbing and closing the game. Few options for audio/gameplay/video settings.
Conclusion:
This game is amazing. I seen a dev gameplay preview months and months ago and didnt think much of it. It just looked like a couple players tethered together and terraforming stuff. Once I purchased the game for my friend and I, I was blown away with how in depth the game got and how much content was available for being EA. Im generally a FPS and MMORPG player so I dont generally play these game but I am more than impressed. Make your own conclusions but I think anybody can get many hours of fun out of this game.

Let me just start this by saying: I'm having fun with this game. Well, I was, anyway. The system requirements are questionable as to whether they'll get you a working 640x480 or a stuttering mess at times. The game can be cheap as hell. It requiring fine responses from you but it can be a flip of a coin at times whether it will accept important dodge moves or just ignore them. Hit detection can be all over the place, with a chainsaw holding enemy managing to hit without their weapon making contact, or miss while the chainsaw goes through Dante. The level design can be confusing, with times all I could think was "What do you want from me?" as I try to determine where the next neatly disguised platform has been hidden, resulting in not even realising which order the game was after. The method of accessing platforms (one grappling hook for pulling them out, one for pulling Dante to them) seems confusing as to when it will decide to acknowledge Dante is in a suitable place. And the sections where Dante has to outrun walls closing in can be nightmarish in its' ignoring attempts to jump and furthering the need for good reaction times. The end result is a game that takes your health for its' inability to follow through on jumping (a fall "off the map" costs Dante health) and dodging, then penalises you for using items to heal that health. A game that confuses with poorly designed platforming sections and things to hit on the wall, then takes away score for taking a while to work out what comes next. A game that makes some enemies a chore (the afforementioned chainsaw weilding ones, anything in the air that requires a lock on that ends with the game focusing Dante on the wrong enemies), then you lose score if you shoot at them because it's the only way the game won't play cheap and steal health and cause frustration through making it far more dangerous to Dante's health than actually fighting against them would be without all the issues mentioned here. That's saying nothing for the maybe 15 frames per second I'm getting or the 5 seconds where the game will just stop in some areas (I think when it's trying to do pop-in of partially transparent character models in a wide space), including during battle.
The game can be fun, at times. It's a lot more whimsical than previous entries and feels more enjoyable (as someone who has played previous Devil May Cry games), with a plot that helps keep up the interest. But it's getting more of a chore than it may be worth for me now, what with the unfair mess it has turned into.
Not recommended.

It's a great game once you get the hang of it and overlook all of the bugs streaming down your way. However, this game's developers don't make it any easier to do so.
There's no tutorial, no manual, no in-game help, no introduction to the game. If you want to seek help, the only thing they provide is a wiki that barely covers the core aspects of the game. I found myself bound to an online search engine in another monitor most of the time, since using the builtin web browser pauses the game that already runs at a slow pace even at the fastest settings. It took me six tries just to find out I could set prisoner intake to zero while I'm still building my jail.
Even though this seems like a game made for PC, there are no customizable keyboard shortcuts. There is no list of preset shortcuts either, so I suggest anyone playing this game to make a cheat sheet as soon as possible.
The AI is mostly fine and on par with this genre's competitors, which is a relief, since you bear no resemblance of control over it. You can't see what they're thinking, they aren't grouped in any in-game listings, you don't even get to assign them to a cell of your choosing.
Even then, the game would still be playable - and fun - if it wasn't for the constant flood of bugs shoved down your face every time. The cleaning cupboard requires a 5x5 room fully enclosed by walls to allow you to assign prisoners to work on it, but the game claims it only needs 3x3 and no walls. Whenever you use the mouse-drag function, be sure to double-check whether or not the game actually completed the rectangle you wanted it to do, since it will often leave a single square untouched. The clone tool only allows you to duplicate a small area, and it will move the area once it reaches the max with no kind of warning. The staff door is just a suggestion, don't take it seriously. It will prevent prisoners from escaping, sure, but, if you mean to prevent their access to dangerous facilities (such as the kitchen), it won't work. This game is a big fan of numbers: two small kitchens will work better than a single big kitchen; two staff rooms will heal your employees a lot faster than a single big staff room. Be careful when building foundations: don't build anything until they're completed and you are sure of it. If a single square was left unfinished and you made the mistake of building a wall around it, you're better off just bulldozing everything and building it again. There's no way to find which spot rendered the entire foundation useless, and, until you do, you can't assign any rooms over it.
In the end, it's a very frustrating experience, because the game could have been a lot of fun: the design was there, but execution was the major letdown. The simulation is deep and comprehensive, demanding a lot of confluent macro and micromanaging, but the replay factor sinks when you remember how many bugs you'd have to face if you were to play it again.

 Borderlands 2 is an action role-playing first-person shooter video game developed by Gearbox Software and published by 2K Games. It is the second game in the Borderlands series and the sequel to 2009's Borderlands. The game was released for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and OS X on September 18, 2012. It was ported to the PlayStation Vita on May 13, 2014, and released for Linux on September 30, 2014.
As with the first game, Borderlands 2 allows players to complete a campaign consisting of central quests and optional side-missions as one of four treasure seekers, "Vault Hunters", on the planet Pandora. Key gameplay features from the original game, such as online collaborative campaign gameplay; randomly generated loot, such as weapons and shields; and character-building elements commonly found in role-playing video games are in Borderlands 2.
The game was well received by critics and was a financial success. Downloadable content for the game was released, including new characters and storylines. The Game of the Year Edition of the game was released in October 8, 2013 in the U.S. and October 11 internationally, including all the previous downloadable and upgrade packs except for the new campaign. A PlayStation Vita version was released in May 2014, and was developed by Iron Galaxy Studios in collaboration with Gearbox. PlayStation 4 and Xbox One ports of Borderlands 2 and its DLC were released as part of Borderlands: The Handsome Collection on March 24, 2015. Borderlands 2 had sold over 13 million copies, making it 2K's highest-selling title.
Gameplay
Borderlands 2s gameplay is similar to its predecessor, with a focus on the completion of missions and the collection of randomly generated "loot"  with various rarities, statistics, and elemental effects. Four playable character classes are available in the base game, each with their own unique abilities and skill trees: Axton, "the Commando", can summon a turret to provide offensive support. Maya, "the Siren", can "phaselock" enemies by trapping them in a sphere of energy for a few seconds. Zer0, "the Assassin", can temporarily become invisible and spawn a hologram decoy to distract enemies; an attack delivered in this state provides bonus damage. Salvador, "the Gunzerker", can use his titular ability to temporarily dual-wield weapons.
New gameplay elements added to Borderlands 2 include a trading system during multiplayer play; slag, a substance that increases damage to targets that are covered in it; new "E-Tech" weaponry; Eridium bars, a new currency for purchasing storage upgrades and other premium items; and the "Secret Stash," a small storage area for transferring items between characters. Increased character customization options were also made available, with collectable items unlocking different character head designs, color schemes, and vehicle paint schemes. A major addition to the game is the "Badass Rank" system; points are awarded for completing various in-game challenges, which in turn award tokens that can be redeemed to increase the player's base stats. These stat improvements apply to all of a single player's characters.
Similarly to the original, completing the main story campaign unlocks "True Vault Hunter Mode", a New Game Plus which increases the difficulty of the game by making enemies stronger, accordingly improves the probability of finding rare and higher-quality items, and allows the player's character to reach level 50. There is also an "Ultimate Vault Hunter Mode" that spawns more difficult enemies and also increases the probability of rare item drops. This mode also raises the level cap to level 72.
Plot
Setting
Five years have passed since the events of Borderlands, when the four Vault Hunters, Roland, Mordecai, Lilith, and Brick were guided by a mysterious entity known as "The Guardian Angel" on the planet of Pandora to the Vault, a mysterious alien structure that was rumored to hold ancient and exotic technology and riches. Instead, these Vault Hunters were confronted by an alien abomination known as "The Destroyer" inside the Vault. After defeating The Destroyer, a valuable mineral called "Eridium" started flourishing through Pandora's crust. Handsome Jack, the president of the Hyperion Corporation, secures this new resource and makes use of it to attempt to "bring peace" to the planet. Now, Handsome Jack rules over the inhabitants of Pandora with an iron fist from his massive satellite built in the shape of an "H", always visible in the sky in front of Pandora's moon. Meanwhile, rumors of an even larger Vault hidden on Pandora spread across the galaxy, drawing a new group of Vault Hunters to the planet in search of it.
Story
The opening cutscene introduces the four new Vault Hunters as they ride a train on Pandora. However, the train is a trap set by Handsome Jack, and it explodes. The Vault Hunters regain consciousness in a frozen wasteland and are found by the last remaining Hyperion CL4P-TP  unit. The Guardian Angel contacts the Vault Hunters and instructs them to accompany Claptrap to the city of Sanctuary, and to join the Crimson Raiders, an anti-Hyperion resistance movement, in order to defeat Handsome Jack. Claptrap and the Vault Hunters are able to escape the frozen wastes after defeating Captain Flynt, the local bandit leader, and retaking Claptrap's boat. Along the way, Handsome Jack taunts the Vault Hunters, while the Guardian Angel offers advice and comfort.
Upon arriving at the gates of Sanctuary, the Vault Hunters are asked to rescue Roland, now leader of the Crimson Raiders, who has been captured by a bounty hunter called the Firehawk. The Vault Hunters meet the Firehawk, who turns out to be Lilith, whose powers as a siren have been significantly enhanced by the new supply of eridium. Lilith informs the Vault Hunters that Roland was actually captured by a group of bandits. After fighting through the bandits' territory, the Vault Hunters rescue Roland and return to Sanctuary.
Roland and Lilith learn that the Vault Key is being transported aboard a Hyperion train, and task the Vault Hunters to retrieve it. To accomplish the mission, the Vault Hunters enlist the aid of former Vault Hunter Mordecai, and of Tiny Tina, a psychotic explosives-obsessed thirteen-year-old. The Vault Hunters derail the train, but instead of finding the Vault Key, they encounter Wilhelm, a powerful Hyperion cyborg. After Wilhelm's defeat, the Vault Hunters recover his power core, which Roland recommends be used as the power source for Sanctuary's shields. The power core turns out to be a trap; it allows the Guardian Angel, who is actually working for Jack, to lower the city's shields and render it vulnerable to a bombardment from the Hyperion moon satellite. Lilith saves Sanctuary, which was originally a large spacecraft, by activating its engines and teleporting it away; for the rest of the game, Sanctuary exists as a flying city in the sky.
Jack's true plan is revealed: to open Pandora's second Vault and unleash The Warrior, a powerful lava, eridium, and rock creature controlled by whomever releases it. Additionally, he is forcing Angel to help him charge the Vault Key more quickly than usual. Angel communicates with the group in Sanctuary, and despite hostile treatment from Roland, divulges that the Vault Key is kept with her in a Hyperion facility. She also shares information about the formidable defenses of the facility. The Vault Hunters embark upon a series of missions in order to assemble what is needed to overcome these defenses, including obtaining an upgrade for Claptrap, visiting the Hyperion city of Opportunity, and enlisting the aid of Brick, now leader of the Slab clan of bandits. One of the most fantastic FPS games I've played! Its cartoon graphics are really amazing, which only helps to make this game unique!
While Skyrim, in my opinion, is the best RPG that incorporates FPS elements, Borderlands is the best FPS with RPG characteristics (XP, leveling, skills, items with numerical attributes). The game is really huge, specially considering the optional quests and the DLCs, that are surprisingly enormous! It is a kind of Far Cry, but much more exciting and miscellaneous!
You can experience 6 different character classes (in GOTY edition) and in 2 different game modes: single and cooperative multiplayer. The first one is more slow and technical, in which you'll need to search better ways to defeat the enemies, since having your health depleted is quite a problem; while the second one is faster and insane! As more users join the game, more "run into the action and fire, fire, fire!" the game will be - you'll need to exit from your cover at least to help fallen friends in order to avoid their deaths! The cooperative mechanism of the game is awesome! The best part is that it is possible to use the same characters (a.k.a. vault-hunters) in either single or cooperative game.
The unique annoying aspect, for me, is the excessive looting and the need of farming during all the time, searching for better items. It reminds me of Diablo a lot, that is a game completely dependent on farming, what displeases me after some game playing.
The game is too cheap (with sales up to 80% off sometimes during the year) for the fun it is able to grant. One of the best aquisitions I've made. I'll buy the Borderlands Pre-Sequel in a near future, for sure! But, for while, I want to explore deeper what Borderlands 2 has to offer! After finish the game with a character, you'll have the possibility of replay it in hardest difficulties to keep your vault-hunter evolving. Almost infinite joy!

There are plenty of things wrong with this game but in spite of this APB: Reloaded remains one of my all time most enjoyable games to play with friends.
Regardless of what most negative reviews will say this game is not pay to win. Cheats have been an issue for years though, and only recently has there been any significant response from Gamers First to combat them.
The biggest issue with the game is the matchmaking system, although it may work on a high populated game there just aren't enough players to split across 3 threat levels. Gold ranked districts are seldom active so even if they do not wish to gold ranked players are forced to "de-threat" by playing bad till they become silver. Once these gold players are silver ranked they can play in the bronze districts till they log out and are not even forcibly removed once they reach gold again. As a result new players are thrown in at the deep end quite early in their APB career and quickly find they're out-matched and out-gunned.
If you're a hardcore first person or third person shooter fan you'll likely not enjoy this game. If you intend to play solo you will likely not enjoy this game. If however you have 1-3 friends to play with and are capable of not taking the game too seriously it's worthy of a download.

If you enjoy watching pros play this game on Youtube, then keep watching it on Youtube. Playing the game itself is a much different experience and I heavily regret dropping 33 bucks into this game. It's NOT READY. Not even close. It has a really long way to go before it's servicable and in its current state, 22$ CAD is way too much. This shouldn't be priced anywhere above 10$ because the value just isn't there. People are gonna call you salty if you get mad at this game. You will get mad, you will be salty and if you lose too many fights and lose too many bases you're gonna finally be humble enough to walk away from this game like I did. I have some bullet points explaing my issues with this game but I'll be less formal to start. The people on this game aren't "funny" like you've seen in youtube videos, they don't talk to eachother. They kill eachother. This game is not noob friendly. Everything and everyone is going to try to kill you and take everything you own and burn down what they can't take with them. And they will succeed. You will die, a lot. I have no problem with the developers of this game. They've made a decent game that is a little overpriced and visibly unfinished. It is the community that butchers any sense of enjoyment. I thought it was funny at first how toxic it was. But it is too toxic. And yes, I am salty.
1. Toxic Community (the sALT)
Players in Rust are hostile, offensive and above all else...SALTY. Some encounters with players can by pleasant but it's mostly people killing eachother over resources (which is a traumatic experience, given how hard it is to gather much of anything). Most conversations between players are people blasting music over their mic, players swearing and saying some pretty racist things and threats of real life violence. None of this is surprising apart from the racism and swearing since servers claim to have banned this behaviour. If they have then they've done a pretty terrible job so far.
2. PVP combat (slow, clunky, laggy)
The combat looks absolutely stupid. It's looks like gmod character models swinging rubber crowbars while jumping and strafing as best as the engine can handle it. Frame drops and lag issues tend to ruin fights and doesn't pair well with the slow, clunky movement controls. Most weapons lack any feeling of impact apart from some guns which actually control and handle pretty well. The issue with that is that guns are SO difficult to come by so you'll be getting shot with them more than you'll actually be holding one.
3. Resources gathering (Minecraft did it better)
Gathering wood and stone to make your first house takes RIDICULOUSLY long. Hatchets/Picks, foundations/walls/roofs and upgrading them to stone costs a LOT of resources. Actually mining all of it to make a solid base can potentially lead up to 1/2 an hour to a full hour of JUST grinding. For this reason, the stakes of fights with other players are just too high. If you lose a fight after grinding enough to build a house then you've lost a half hour at least. And if you couldn't find enough cloth to make a sleeping bag then you'll be respawned on the other side of the map. Good luck there.
4. Raids (offline raids, accesible to few)
ALL of the the raids I experienced happened offline. Around 2:00Am to 4:00Am was primetime for people to often blow open my front door and chop my body and sleeping bag and clear my house of all loot and furnishings. Raiding other people takes explosives or serious mining tools which, let's be honest. Unless you have a clan or a friend or two who are masters at this game and know where to look for the right components, you're not making these anytime soon, So raiding is only for the rich to grief the less fortunate.
5. No room for nakeds (noob killing, no tutorials)
This is actually a phenomenon that I don't see in a lot of other games. Sure enough call of duty/battlefield/any multiplayer game makes fun of noobs but usually there are a few people willing to teach someone the ropes. But Rust treats noobs horribly. People often camp the beaches and shoot new players who have just spawned in. There isn't a tutorial or any fellow players to teach nakeds how to even play the game so they're thrust into the game world where they're killed for sport over and over again. I understand the idea of "earning the right to be good" through player encounters and getting in fights but that doesn't work when people with guns are shooting you for your rock and torch.
If you havent heard of it yet, Ark is another survival game. It looks like clans are easier to join and that there is a little less player interaction since a large focus of the game is NPC dinosaurs that you can tame.It too seems overpriced at 80$ Canadian but it has some semblance of finish to it. It has many of the same problems from what I can tell but what I do know is that in terms of survival games, Rust still has a long way to go. Don't waste your time or money here, there are better games that can offer a much better expierience at a better price. Hopefully in a few years this game is finished but the community isn't going to be changing anytime soon. Stay salty.

So, I discovered Agent 47 with Absolution, then, by curiosity, I bought Blood Money, and then Silent Assassin and came to the conclusion: Absolution is a good game but not a good Hitman.
And here we are.
Hitman (2016) is a stealth game where you play as a cold blooded assassin named Agent 47 because real names are overrated.
The game is divided in 7 episodes, or levels, that take place around the world.
First, good ole' baguette land: France, then, Italy, Morroco, Thailand, 'Murica and Japan.
Of course, fellow average internet user! Though I'm just not counting the tutorial you are right.
Since this game is not about an overall game with a main story developing in each level, I won't make a big review on the game, but mini reviews on each level.
Paris:
"Can't acces to Eiffel Tower"-0/10 IGN
So Paris was the first level realeased in HITMAN. It is pretty classic when you look at the other levels, but god it is a good first impression. About 20 ways to assassinate the targets, all pretty damn satisfaying to pull off. Poisoning is the easiest but most un-satisfiying kill of all and if you get into it, we have really good assassinations. Good level overall.
Sappienza:
The best level for many, wich I can understand. The level is beautiful, and like the rest of the levels the assassinations are good and all different from one another. Nothing more to say.
Marrakech:
A very open level, though you will get lost in your first tries, once you know everything, it's a fun level.
I mean, you can throw an army general in the printer that makes his own propaganda (Oh the irony!), isn't that good enough for you?
Bangcock:
A good part of the community don't like this level, and really, it's again a good level! I see it as better Paris, because the level is one big hotel, and Paris is one big palace/fashion show.
Colorado:
Probably the worst level. Not worst like "That sucks" but it's the least good level of all this season. The fact that there are 5 objectives and 4 targets didn't give enough room to the developpers, so the assassinations are not very creative and 3/4 of the trophies (In the assassination category) will be to kill them all in a commune way in one run, like poison. But the plot twist at the end is a little interesting at least.
Hokkaido:
My favorite level as a certified weeb. So we have 2 parts: the High-Tech part of the level and the entertainment/traditional part, and both have their targets. The assassinations are really interesting and the Mastery-Level 20 Sniper is a must have.
The game itself is really good, even the tutorial has replay value!
For me it is the best Hitman so far, and I am waiting for season 2, hoping for the same quality.
Also, if you have it, make your friend/brother/sister play it. It's always a pleasure to see someone doing there first run on levels.

This is the app this game needs, but is it app this game deserves? Reviewing both the game itself and the PC adaptation.
PROS:
- Unique, challenging villians that create interesting thematic challenges.
- High difficulty ensures replayability. Game is not easily solvable.
- Computer does all the game's bookkeeping for you.
- Heroes and variants add onto gameplay variety.
CONS:
- Overwhelming number of modifiers and conditions to monitor. Things can get out of hand very quickly and it becomes difficult to work out what's happening in a turn.
- Environments feel tacked on and don't evoke the setting they're trying to protray.
- The game's mechanics drive the intensity of a match down. Things start of engaging and interesting, then become routine and formality as the Heroes finally get control of the situation.
- Actual meaningful choice during a match is rare. Most decisions are just tests of your ability to calculate the optimal move.
- Art is inconsisent and leans towards sloppy.
PURCHASE CONSIDERATION TIDBIT:
Core game feels a bit anemic. I'd advise buying at least one season alongside the core if this is a game that appeals to you.
Would Recommend To:
Comic book readers who are into turn based games and who are already familiar with the term "order of operations."
Would Alternatively Suggest:
PC Game Alternatives: Yomi (Dueling card game with cleaner mechanics and similar pay model), Tabletop Simulator with any of the games below.
Board/Card Game Alternatives: Battlecon (Competitive turn based 1v1 fighting card game, dripping with theme and meaningful decision driven gameplay). Legendary or DC Comics Deck Building game (Licensed superhero card game. Theme is not delivered as well as Sentinels, but the games compensate by providing more interesting options during gameplay than Sentinels).
Will thumb up ultimately because there's not a lot of PC accessible superhero card games and it is a fun game to play, despite it flaws. However, if any of my board game alternatives ever become a full fledged PC app themselves, I would thumb down this game for those alternative instead.

There are plenty of things wrong with this game but in spite of this APB: Reloaded remains one of my all time most enjoyable games to play with friends.
Regardless of what most negative reviews will say this game is not pay to win. Cheats have been an issue for years though, and only recently has there been any significant response from Gamers First to combat them.
The biggest issue with the game is the matchmaking system, although it may work on a high populated game there just aren't enough players to split across 3 threat levels. Gold ranked districts are seldom active so even if they do not wish to gold ranked players are forced to "de-threat" by playing bad till they become silver. Once these gold players are silver ranked they can play in the bronze districts till they log out and are not even forcibly removed once they reach gold again. As a result new players are thrown in at the deep end quite early in their APB career and quickly find they're out-matched and out-gunned.
If you're a hardcore first person or third person shooter fan you'll likely not enjoy this game. If you intend to play solo you will likely not enjoy this game. If however you have 1-3 friends to play with and are capable of not taking the game too seriously it's worthy of a download.

My first 150 hours of Rust have been incredibly enjoyable.
The gameplay isn't hard to get into once you know the basics, but there's always another way to do something better than before, and I really like that the PvP element pushes you to learn from your mistakes and improve your methods, whether it's constructing your base more efficiently or moving and dodging more effectively. What's more is that Rust continues to evolve with each update released. I'm always finding new ways to build bases and traps, and new tactics to outplay the people who live around me - and the updates just keep introducing new possibilities and styles of play. What makes Rust so good (in my opinion) is that it doesn't force you to play a certain way. Sure, you can go all-out with a big group and big guns, but if you'd rather trick your opponents and lure them into devious traps or ambush them while they're doing a recycling run, you can do that. The community continues to amaze me with unique tactics - you never know what to expect from another player.
While the visuals aren't exactly next-gen, they are VERY pretty and the sounds really match the ambience of the the overall game. Sitting in your base next to a barbeque while the sun sets and listening to the subtle crackling of the charcoal, or rustling through bushes in the pitch-black darkness of night and watching the moon-lit silhoutte of a deer on the horizon - it's beautiful.
I've heard many negative things about the recent twig and blueprint updates, and I too was sceptical at first, but after playing through it, I can wholeheartedly say that I support these changes and I think they really help the early-game stages stretch out - which is something that I feel is necessary for a survival game like Rust. I love that the team is still working hard on the game and producing regular updates with new and interesting content.
TL;DR: Great gameplay, great visuals, great fun.

I don’t understand the praise that this game receives. The gameplay is serviceable, but the single player is short, and unsatisfying. When I was confronted with the first major decision in this game, I had an awful thought. That thought was “these choices won’t matter, will they?” After the scene played out I had an even worse thought. That thought was “the big twist better not be that you’re hallucinating.” Guess what? I was right both times. Oops, spoilers. Unless your Mary Shelley, you shouldn’t pull the “protagonist was the monster all along” card. It’s not thought provoking; it’s cliché. Following this reveal, will the final scene in this game end with a gunshot followed by a fade to black? No, but what you get instead is about as engaging. The endings are unsatisfying because your previous “choices” do not determine your fate. Instead, you have four options that determine what happens to Captain Walker. These include, shooting yourself because you’re a nut or shooting your hallucination. Do you get it? Either way, this game is going to blow your mind! Truly, this idea is art at its highest form. There is absolutely no hackery to be seen here. From there you are presented with three more options. These include being a violent nut for no reason, being a violent nut who can’t aim by endgame, or being a nut who does nothing at all. I went with doing nothing at all. You see, I’m a nut of the nonviolent variety. I’m also a sucker, because I bought this game. Whoops.

Just finished this game, and I have to say it is one of the best narrative driven games I've ever played, period. This game explores the role of the player in violence, the horror and mission creep in warfare, and the way in which the circumstances of war can often lead to justifications and dissillusionment that are both harmful and deadly. This game from a narrative standpoint will challenge you like possibly no other game you have played. The writing and plot are flawless. The progression of the main charecters is impressive, both in the degradation of the mental states and the progression of how they feel towards killing.
The level design in this game is some of the best I have ever seen. Not necessarily from the standpoint that it is layered and complex, because it is extremely liniar from a gameplay perspective. But the level design in terms of art, storytelling, and atmosphere is downright incredible. You will find yourself stumbling through the remains of a once great and opulent city. There are details everywhere of the people and life that used to be there. Now it's all buried under sand. The kind of enviorments and structures you find yourself in are varied and engaging, and most importantly tell the story that the narrative is trying to tell you.
My big complaint with this game is the gameplay. Take a watered down, flawed version of the Gears of War combat system, and there you have this game. The cover system is oftentimes infuriating, many times not registering the space bar when you want to take cover or stop running. The execution feature is needlessly brutal and kind of awkwardly thrown in there (some may argue this could be a narrative choice, and I am willing to entertain that point of view). And most importantly, the gameplay is incredibly repetitive and wave based. Which again, people make arguements that this is a narrative choice. That is very possible, but the reality is that with games, the gameplay has to be engaging. If it's just another "Oh♥♥♥♥♥♥ we got Tangos on the way!!! Take cover!!!" over and over again, it's gonna get old after eight hours.
A recommendation I would make is to not play this game on the hardest difficulty. I did that, and I beleive it makes it needlessly frustrating to grind through waves of enemies. It only increases the frustration you will have with a broken cover system and other game mechanics. Play it on normal at least, even easy (although I prefer some challenge, so if I could do it again, I would play it on normal).
All this being said, and some broken mechanics and repetitive gameplay aside, this game is without a doubt a masterpiece akin to Apocolypse Now. I'm gonna be spending a lot of time thinking and reading about this game for awhile. If you enjoy narrative, play this game. It is unmatched.

After Hitman Absolution failed to deliver a quality experience this franchise is known for, I became extremely skeptical of what the next game would have to offer. Couple that with the episodic model and my expectations were at an all time low. As a result, I held off on getting this game for quite a while and only got it once IOI announced they were becoming an independent studio. The fact that by that time HITMAN was a full game and the discount they offered helped a lot in getting me to finally give it a try. I did not regret it.
While it does keep certain mechanics from Absolution, this game is nothing like it. This game once again offers that experience the franchise is known for, only in much larger levels and with better graphics. This is a proper Hitman game - meaning you will be playing large sand-box missions, where you will have to go after at least two targets each and figure out how best to get close to those targets and how best to kill them. And there are quite a few creative ways to kill your targets, some of which may even involve some direct interaction (as in conversations!) between Mr. 47 and a target - an aspect of the game I greatly appreciate, as it has made 47 that much more interesting as a character.
While I still miss Jesper Kyd's music in Hitman, the music in this game is nothing to laugh at and manages to create a unique atmosphere.
David Bateson is once again back as the voice of Mr. 47 and he's still got it. Unfortunately, Diana's actress was changed once again and while the current actress is not bad, Diana's voice and personality seem quite different from the previous games. For me it was a mixed bag, but others might get a different impression.
All in all, HITMAN is a return to form for this franchise that has provided me with many hours of fun. I wholeheartedly recommend it and hope IOI can keep it going with any future installments.

What really shows why this mod doesn't work is the gameplay in the first few minutes. The game is generous at first because it gives you a pistol and an SMG at the very start when the helicopter drops you off, but right as it drops you off (when the cutscene ends) you're placed in an area with tons of combine shooting at you from a distance in all different directions, and you have two weapons meant for close quarters combat. It's an interesting position to be in to be able to judge a reboot of a much-loved game franchise with no knowledge of the games which came before. Such is the case with me and the enigma that is DmC: Devil may Cry. Strange naming aside, this game, despite being much maligned by the Devil May Cry fanbase, is, from a totally objective viewpoint such as mine, still worth a play.
The game's plot reads like Conspiracy theory nine billion and seven - The world has been secretly infiltrated by demons, and a small resistance made up of anti-hero playable character Dante, talented psychic Kat and charismatic leader Vergil is fighting to try and free humanity from their iron-fisted, secret power. The corny underlying plot, however, is tempered slightly by the twists and turns that occur during the plotline, so whilst it may have a bland initial taste it's an alright plot, and definitely not the worst.
The main character, as stated before, is Dante, who starts off as an unlikeable anti-hero but as ther game progresses, he begins to see the importance of his actions, to realise what is at stake if he is to fail - though his desire for justice also has a noticeable streak of revenge running through it. Overall though, he's an interesting character, and the only other gripe I have about him is that his voice acting is somewhat subpar, especially when he's shouting.
What flaws there are are made up fror in the gameplay. At its core it's your typical hack n' slash fare, you have a large, bladed weapon, you can kill enemies with it, and like any good hack & slash it's very, very fun - though this game spices it up a bit by throwing in Ebony and Ivory, a pair of pistols which Dante can use to juggle enemies in the air and hit far-off foes. As you progress through the game Dante also unlocks new weapons, such as Arbiter, a massive demonic axe, Aquila, a pair of glaives, and Revenant, a powerful shotgun. These weapons allow for more interesting gameplay by allowing one to juggle multiple weapons tactically to finish off enemies effectively, making the gameplay all the more fun, and as it is with most hack and slashes, it's really fun to hack and slash the living daylights out of many enemies at a time.
In summary, in spite of its shortcomings, DmC: Devil may Cry is a good game for its genre. With a slightly-cheesy, yet interesting plot, believable characters and gameplay which builds a bit on the classic hack n' slash formula, it's definitely worth a play, even if you HAVE played a DmC game before.

Looking through my reviews I noticed this one and realized it was not very good. I only offered a few of the many issues I had with the game. I feel as though I can do better explaining my issues with this game now.
---
As a fan of this series I was quite heavily disappointed by this game. As a stand alone it would've been okay, at least tolerable. There was no reason to slap Devil May Cry onto the game. Leaving such big shoes to fill and then completely failing to fulfill expectations is like a punch to the face.
Story and Characters:
The DMC story and lore is quite interesting. It is a world where one of the strongest Demons, Sparda forced all demons back to their world and then seperated the two worlds with his power. In the process he lost his powers and even then continued to fight for justice for humanity until his eventual death. Before his death, having two sons- Vergil and Dante.
This reboot throws that interesting story out of the window. DmC took one of the most important characters and ruined him. Sparda in this story is a wimpy demon who had kids with an angel. When Mundus finds out he locks up and humiliates Sparda for the rest of eternity. How could Ninja Theory do this? This is such a huge shift in character and a major issue. In the previous games Dante had the power to take on Mundus because his relation to Sparda and the power he had. However this wimpy Sparda could never hope to stand up to Mundus. Where does DmC Dante get the power to defeat Mundus? Don't try to say that his demon/angel combination of blood made him stronger. Because even if that were true there would be nothing special about Sparda's blood if he's so utterly weaker than Mundus. There is really no reason for Dante to be strong other than Ninja Theory just stating that "Nephilim are strong". No setup as to why Nephilim are so great, it's just stated.
DmC Dante is another character issue. Ninja Theory went complete opposite of DMC Dante. DMC Dante was fun loving, wild, witty, and over the top. DmC Dante is what happens when game devs ask what a 10 year old CoD player thinks is cool. Edgy, vulgar and boring. Most dialogue goes as follows: "♥♥♥♥ you" "No, ♥♥♥♥ you", repeat.
Vergil is the worst part. Where as DMC Vergil is an honorable warrior who does not use firearms, never attacks from behind, and never fights dirty. Ninja Theory threw all that out the window. DmC Vergil does sniper rifle abortions from a hiding spot on demon mothers. Even after bargaining for peace. Really Ninja Theory? Really? Couldn't think of a way to get any edgier? So you moved to Vergil killing unborn demon babies? Kills me to see them do this to the series. Even if it is a reboot. Also that ending was really unexplained. Vergil suddenly loses it, says that he wants to rule over humanity in Mundus' place and then fights Dante. At least DMC3 explained why Vergil did all he did. Vergil suddenly does a 180 within the last 5 minutes of the game.
Kat is Kat. The game would have been the same if she hadn't been in it, she brought almost nothing to the table but semi forced Dante romance and weird Vergil idolization.
Mundus is the only decent character in the game. Biggest issue is him is that why is he trying to take over the world using economics and brainwashing? Why doesn't he use his extremely powerful demon powers to force everyone and everything to his will. Really absurd.
Dialogue is terrifying, almost as if it was written by a really edgy preteen. Dropping vulgarities like it's going out of style does not make a game cool. Really fun drinking game- take a shot every time Dante or someone else curses. Proceed to die of alcohol poisoning.
Gameplay:
Extremely important aspect of a third person hack and slash, also the key point of the entire DMC series. DMC gameplay has always been smooth, combo oriented, style heavy, and complex.
DmC is none of this. Combos are often broken up by angel/demon enemies. These enemies require you to use angel/demon weapons on them. You'll be in a combo fighting an enemy and suddenly one of these guys will jump in front of you, you'll hit them with the wrong weapon since you're in the middle of doing a move against the original standard enemy and your combo will break. In a game about combos this is not good. It breaks the flow of combat to be required to use a specific weapon against a specific enemy.
Combat has been "dumbed down". Lack of a lock on contributes. Ninja Theory expected that just hitting the nearest enemy would be good enough and that lock on wouldn't be necessary. Ha ha ha ha... Yeah... No... Achieving high style levels are easier than ever. In prior DMC games you had to introduce variety to your combos in order to get high ranks. You couldn't spam "YYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY+" to get SSS. But you bet you can do that in DmC, I tried. It worked. Got to SSS by spamming standard attack.
DT is also extremely silly. In old DMC games DT changed the characters appearance, made their attacks stronger and faster, evasive moves more effective while maintaining the enemy's strength. DmC DT just nerfs the enemy. It doesn't buff you, make your attacks stronger or faster. It stops time and throws the enemies into the air making them defenseless. How is that a challenge or fun? When DT'd in DMC you still had to keep an eye out for enemies because no matter how awesome DT made you, the enemies were still putting up a fight.
Where are the projectile weapons? All you get are Ebony+Ivory. Where's my shotgun? Where's Pandora?
No Turbo mode is just depressing. Don't tell me to buy Definitive Edition because it contains all the garbage that should've been in the original game. Funny how Definitive Edition adds mechanics that DMC games had. HMMMMMMMM.....?
This game is just so easy. Even the hardest difficulty of DmC barely touches Dante Must Die or normal mode in the other DMC games. Boss fights were the most disappointing part, they barely put up a fight.
Optimization:
Game worked fine, looked fine and even had beautiful backgrounds in some places. That's the only compliment I can give this game. Looks beautiful in places. Shame the story and gameplay sours it.
Overall:
Ninja Theory searched for ways to be drastically different from the old DMC games and in their pursuit to be drastically different they forgot the reason the other games were so great. They lost sight of the original material and made a mess of this reboot. I'd be completely okay if I never saw a sequel for this game.
I recommend no fan of the DMC series purchase this game. This is not for you.
I'd give this game a 1/10.
