Review written on 07/29/14:
I've been playing APB Reloaded since it was in Open Beta, back around late 2011. Since then, I've logged over 2,000 hours on my main character, who is a max rank gold, AgentRick (Enforcer, Joker East).
APB: Reloaded, like many other games, has it's ups and downs, but it's an extremely unique game that allows you to do so much more than any other game out there.
Let's look at customization first, since this is probably the most significant differentiator that APB: Reloaded has to offer. They have a detailed designer that allows you to make practically anything in-game utilizing tools and presets ranging from basic shapes, to gradients, and even masking tools to allow for cropping of symbols. If you're a premium player, you are able to customize your character and vehicle with unbelievable detail. My clan currently utilizes a Sheriff's Office theme and we have extremely detailed vehicles, uniforms, and logos.
Next, let's have a look at gameplay. The matchmaking system in place may not be the greatest at this current moment, but there is a visible effort on GamersFirst's part to tweak the matchmaking engine, and it's especially evident with the release of the Open Conflict districts. In comparison to Open Beta, the matchmaking system and the balance of mission objectives have come a long way. It's also evident that GamersFirst does focus on working out kinks in the system, as I personally worked with several GMs to eliminate the "No-Witness-Zone" bug from the Waterfront Districts about a year ago.
Many people complain about the Armas Marketplace, but what they don't understand is that the Armas Marketplace, which allows you to purchase weapons, special clothing, special vehicles, and premium, is APB Reloadad's source of income. I have yet to see or hear an advertisement in APB: Reloaded from a real-world company that paid for it's logo to be placed in APB. (I have seen this in a number of other games)
The weapons that you can purchase in the Armas Marketplace, although some being unique and only available through Armas at this time, aren't very overpowered. Many people may not know this, but many of the Armas Weapons are simply permanent versions of existing weapons and reskins of existing weapons. Skill plays a MASSIVE role in APB: Reloaded, which many people fail to understand. Every weapon, Armas or not, has a specific purpose, some being more flexible than others.
If you are a brand new player, and don't purchase Armas Weapons right off the get-go, things may be slightly more difficult for you if you were to be put up against someone who has for instance. If you're willing to stick the hardship out for a short period of time, you'll find that you'll be unlocking weapons that are just as good, and as you develop your skills in the game, you'll learn tactics and gain proficiency with your favorite weapon(s).
I own an account-bound permanent weapon that people seem to complain about as being overpowered on a regular basis- the ACES Rifle. Although the ACES Rifle has a fast firing rate and decent range, it's not impossible to beat, as one of my own clanmates was able to take me down a number of times with his stock OCA. As I had mentioned above, APB is more of a skill-based game than anything, and typically whoever lands their shots, and lands the first shots, has a better chance at killing the other player, regardless of the weapon. Look at those (myself included) who have gone CQB with the PSR "Harrier", (A reskin of the N-HVR 762) against someone using, say, an OCA. If I land my two shots before they land their 8 shots, they're dead. Thus, entering into the next section of this review, the community.
The community of players in APB: Reloaded are quite unique. You'll find that although there are a number of trolls and a quite a few sub-par players who will frequently smear and accuse good players of cheating, that you will meet some pretty nice people on APB. The troll and raging 12 year old population on APB isn't as significant as it is on games such as those from the Call of Duty series.
Being that I've logged over 2,000 hours on my primary character alone, I've seen quite a number of things happen in APB. I've also been accused of using some pretty ridiculous non-existent cheats in the game. (Such as increased weapon damage cheats, increased health cheats, etc.) Although this can be discouraging for skilled players, especially if/when you become questioned or reviewed by someone more important than a raging 12 year old, it certainly isn't a big enough deterrent not to play the game.
My biggest recommendations to any and all new players to APB are quite simple.
1) There are threat levels, identified by color. (Trainee/Green, Bronze, Silver, and Gold) The APB Districts are segregated by threat level, and players can play in servers equal to, or one below their threat level. If you are silver, play in bronze districts. Due to the fact that people don't normally populate gold districts, you'll see a lot of golds in the silver districts.
2) If you have a friend who got you into the game, and they're a gold player, ask them to make a reroll account to help you in the beginning. Trust me, grouping with a gold player when you're brand new is being thrown right into the fire, and it will only frustrate you and make you want to quit the game. This again goes back to number one, play with or below your threat level in the beginning.
3) Understand that there have been people who have been playing this game for a very long time and have a lot of experience playing it. Don't assume that because someone is better than you (especially if you're new for goodness sakes) that they must be hacking. Everyone, myself included, has players that are better than them in APB. It's a fact of life- accept this fact, and you'll enjoy the game a lot more.
4) Join a clan!!! There are plenty of clans out there in APB: Reloaded. If you want to make the best of your game experience, join a clan! Find a group of people who you can play with, have fun with, and who can teach you the ropes. It's much easier to play with an organized group and you're more likely to win your missions if you do so. (Teamwork and Communication are MASSIVE force multipliers in APB: Reloaded, as they are in just about every game. A well-organized team of silvers can easily defeat a non-organized team of golds of equal rank.)
5) Know that you can do things other than playing missions! Although a lot of experienced gold players play in the Fight Clubs, Fight Club is a great way for players to hone their skills. It may not be the best learning option in the beginning, but I promise if you play Fight Club for a day straight once you've got the basics of the game down, you'll learn A LOT!
If you start to get upset with missions or fight club, go to social district and talk to people. There are a number of quite funny people who hang around social. If you're a criminal, why not try your hand at ramraiding? It can be both relaxing and rewarding. If you're new, and you decide to ramraid, go to a LOW population server (I'm talking the lowest possible population with the closest match to your threat level.)
Be creative! Mess around in the designers. Make some symbols or themes. Look on youtube for some tutorials on how to use the editors and hone your skills at designing. That can make you a nice amount of money, and it's always pretty cool to see someone randomly driving down the street in a car you designed and sold!
6) Have fun with the game! If you like it, help support the game by getting premium. Even if you were to only purchase premium once, you'd have the ability to fully customize your clothes and vehicles, and they'll stay that way when your premium runs out.
Although I've had ups and downs in APB over the years, I'd definitely say that APB is a game worth picking up and playing for a while. What do you have to lose?

I played this game numerous times when it came out. I loved it then, and I love it now. This time I have discovered a bug/exploit that might be helpful to survivor players. The bug involves the hide in shadows skill. When in a dungeon or at night outside, you can target an enemy and then activate your hide in shadows, the glitch is you become totally invisible, and can maintain attack in this state for as long as you like. It doesn't drain stamina. The catch is to deactivate it you have to find a light source. This is usually pretty easy to accomplish by the numerous torches and piles of gold littering a dungeon. If you don't want to look around, carry a ruby or other gem and just drop it, it will provide enough light to cancel the shadows.

I generally play action RPGs or just RPGs (souls series, witcher, elder scrolls, fallout etc.) and I've found some phenominal titles. Might as well have been another episode to HL2.  MINERVA was a very enjoyable experience that didn't necessarily introduce anything new but is of such high quality that it's difficult to remember that it wasn't made my the developers themselves.  Well, I suppose it was, as this mod was so damn good it got the dude a position at Valve...
What narrative that exists is told in a very subtle HL fashion.  I found it to be very interesting and moving.
Action was superb.  Pacing was very similar to how it was in HL2 so you never get too tired of this.
Puzzles were minimal at best, but they exist and they're believable while still contributing to the atmosphere.
Level design is what makes this mod stand out.  I guess the creator used an approach that revolved around efficient use of space rather than expanding the levels on the X axis; you therefore have very small, tightly-packed levels that are well designed and have more use of verticality than you would typically see in a game.
Overall I liked it very much.  Fantastic mod, and I look forward to seeing more of this guy's work.

TL;DR - If you thought Diablo II was too small and needed more freedom in character customization, you'll probably love this game.
Divine Divinity is an isometric action RPG in the style of Diablo but with some unique differences. First off, the world is fairly large, with open areas to explore and an impressive number of side quests to complete. Dungeons are typically expansive as well - the first major dungeon being at least 3 spawling levels with some sub-areas thrown in too. A number of environment pieces can actually be moved (if it has a weight noted, it can be picked up), which allowed for a nice way to hide items/areas without resorting to locked/secret/illusionary entrances all the time.
DD has you choose a class at the start, but you can select spells/skills from anywhere as you progress, allowing you to hybrid to your heart's content. One of DD's strengths is customization - between charms, stats and skills you have a lot of control over how you want to play your character. That said, there are a few skills that are strong enough to warrant including in any build (and a couple that are required later on to finish some quests), which somewhat detracts from the mix-n-match customization as a whole.
For the most part, the game is non-linear so you can complete and explore as you desire, but you'll find that many locations are way above what you can handle at lower levels. At one point I scoured the countryside killing mobs basically to farm a few levels, which ended up being about 2 nights of gameplay. It was a little annoying that I wasn't working on any major quests at the time, but the map features tons of little interesting areas (most with a small quest/story of their own) which broke up the monotony of level grinding.
There's a fairly large amount of history/lore to back up the main storyline which was adequate and heroic, but I was disappointed with the game's ending (assuming there's only one) as it was a little vague... though I guess that was intentional to allow for sequel potential (which seems to be the case).
Overall Divine Divinity is a solid title in the genre and provides many hours of open-exploration, quest-completing, monster-slaying, loot-obtaining RPG goodness.

Ori and the Blind Forest is a masterpiece.
It's a perfection in everything can be offered by a game, or more accurately, a metroidvania. It has a humongous, continuous map with no in-between screens that sports a stunning visual. It also has an interesting plotline with elegant storytelling and an amazing soundtrack to accompany it all.
Not to mention the gameplay. It has surprisingly DEEP mechanics for a game that seem to focus on aesthetics. While the game is mainly about exploration and puzzle, it can have really interesting combat as well. The odd quirk that this game has is that the further you go in, the easier combat becomes due to the steep increase of mobility with each 'upgrades'. Despite that, the game compensates itself with increasingly challenging deathtraps configuration and strong enemies that each has its own unique combat behavior.
I'd recommend this game to anyone who loves eye candy, challenging gameplay, and good 2D games in general. Mind you, though, this game isn't for the faint of heart (in terms of difficulty!)

Wow. This game was a blast from start to finish.
The game's aesthetics are of an extremely high quality, everything from the visual effects in the menu screens to the unique, intricate art style make this game a breathtaking experience. Some of the best visuals in any game that I've ever seen.
The gameplay is also fluid and entertaining, with the Metroidvania elements ensuring that it never got old or stale, there was always something new to keep my interest. A wide variety of abilities, as well as a 3-Branch skill tree allows a lot of customisation and keeps the combat interesting, as there are many ways that you can defeat enemies. The game's difficulty can be jarring at first, but after enough gameplay and getting used to the moves and controls it becomes much more enjoyable.
The open world map is large and expansive, packed full of secrets and collectibles that add a lot more game-time to the overall experience. A large number of themed "areas" or "levels", are available, the best of which are the "dungeons", which contain some fun and unique puzzle/platforming concepts.
Don't want to spoil anything, but the story is also great, with some minor twists and some tugging of the heartstrings.
Overall, this indie game is easily worth your money, even more so than a lot of AAA titles, simply put, its a masterpiece.

If you look at this game purely from a gameplay perspective, it's an above-average platformer with excellent map design, unique puzzles and some very challenging run sequences. The controls can take some time to get used to (though that may be partly due to my having not played a platformer since New Super Mario Bros. Wii), but once you master them they feel intuitive and tight. Map exploration is in the vein of a classic "Metroidvania," but the plot unfolds in a largely linear fashion so while exploring the world thoroughly can feel rewarding many of the secrets are very predictable in when you'll gain access to them, and there's only one optional area to explore.
But all of that doesn't do any justice to the stunning visuals, the wonderful story, the amazing atmosphere and the godly soundtrack. All of those things combined make this game one of the absolute best I've played in literal years, and one that's more than likely to stand the test of time and remain an amazing game even years later.

Super Meat Boy is an amazingly crafted game. Billed as an ultra-hard platformer, you'll find yourself dying over and over to many of the game's levels. A lot of people don't like stuff like that, but in this game I love it. Since the devs knew you'd constantly be dying, they made you respawn almost instantly, with the music never stopping between attempts. And once you finish the level...? You'll be treated with dozens of your attempts playing at once, instant replay style. It's pretty cool and a neat way to factor the death system into the game's "story".
Wall-jumping is a big part of this game. How you time your trajectory and the speed at which you do so is going to determine how far you make it, especially in the later levels of the game. Thing is, they nailed the platforming here perfectly. It feels so satisfying jumping from wall to wall, landing right on that narrow platform after a well timed jump.
Honestly--platforming at its finest. This game almost turns it into an art.
It does have its flaws though.
In the game, there are these secret areas known as Warp Zones. What's different about these Warp Zones is that unlike the rest of the game, you have lives! And if you run out of lives before completing the set of levels you have to start from the beginning.
I get that they wanted to implement a new type of challenge with these levels, but it goes so against the rest of the game's design. What really bugs me is that you can lose lives on the first level in the sequence, which essentially accomplishes nothing design-wise because getting a game-over on the first level wouldn't make you lose progress anyway.
Still though, I really think this game is something special. If you're a fan of the platforming genre, I think you owe it to yourself to play this game.

I use a lot of photosource for my tiling textures, and this is an amazing tool. It's very intuitive to use after following along with Allegorithmic's video walkthrough, which takes you through all the stuff you need to get started. The normal maps this program generates are miles better than anything Photoshop generates, and you get all the other PBR slots like Height maps, and whatnot, which really pushes the texture to new levels. This is a must buy for anyone serious about environmental art.
The only "gotcha" is that some maps are exported as greysale, which Unity can't read naturally, so you have to change thme to RGB in photoshop, but once you do that you're gold. I plopped everything into the standard shader and after tweaking how intense I wanted each thing to be, it all looked great.

So, before I go any further with my review, full disclosure: I have the card game. I have probably spent 2-300 hours playing the physical game, and I am not exaggerating when I say that it is one my favorite tabletop games of all time. AND I've also kickstarted Season 2 of this game, so there you go--I told you, and I'm not hiding anything!
NOW THEN! On to the review!
Pros:
+This game automates a lot of the functions that go off in the card game, while also explaining them to you, improving your own experience when it comes to the physical game.
+Unique artwork that, as far as I can tell, seems to have been done by the artist for the game (cannot confirm, if someone from Handelabra would let me know, that'd be swell! :D)
+Pleasant music that suits the mood rather well, the vast majority of the time--it helps set the mood with a lot of games, I find.
+It has online multiplayer!
+Very few bugs; I can't think of a single one that I've encountered in my 30+ hours with the title.
Cons:
-Very rarely have I seen anyone playing multiplayer on this game
-Some fights are nearly unwinnable (though, to be fair, that isn't Handelabra's fault, that's more a problem with the design of the card game)
Well, that about sums up my feelings on the game. I'll be honest, it's solid, and if you enjoy the card game, you will enjoy this. However, if you've never played the card game before, I'd highly recommend giving this a look if you're curious about digital card games. The price is right, the company that makes the game is friendly and VERY helpful, and the gameplay loop, while simple, is incredibly addictive and creates that "one more turn" mentality that I get from games like Civ, strangely enough, despite this being an entirely different genre!
So yeah, I cannot praise this game higher. I rate games like this: Buy, wait for sale, or pass, and this game? It gets a 'buy' out of the gate just for being as superb as it is. You wouldn't expect a digital conversion of a card game to have such a nice aesthetic, along with the obvious amount of care and effort that Handelabra has put in on this title. So again, I cannot recommend this game enough.

I made the mistake of ignoring this game and blowing it off as something that I wouldn't be interested in when it popped up Steam awhile back.  I didn't consider myself much of a card game/board game fan and didn't think it would be much fun even though I do enjoy super powered games.

Sentinels of the Multiverse is the best Hero vs. Villain(s) solo/cooperative card game adapted to a digital media out there. Besides the very niched genre it is also a VERY entertaining game with a ludicrous amounts of permutations which I've wasted too many hours on in the little heroes room with my iPad. Getting it on Steam was just a must to support something awesome.
With the upcoming Season 2 content the digital version is going to be even better than the physical version, that tends to be a little too heavy on the bookkeeping side (So many cards! So many stacks!)

The card art is extremely rough around the edges and could probably do with an update someday, but hot damn the mechanics and general feel of the game are well crafted. Honestly the art doesn't detract a lot from the experience and it is all a certain unified comic book style rather than differing per deck, so it's neat how it all ties together.
It's a little plodding in pacing sometimes, and some card actions require a bit of streamlining (you to tell the system to go ahead with a default more than not, in my experience), but generally the game is actually really good fun, The team versus villain thing works well, as it makes the game cooperative with friends (so there's no Mario Party situation of everyone falling out), and having the environment as a deck with its own turn makes things interesting to work with, since you have to keep reacting to both the villain and a general hazard in the background.
The gameplay is pretty solid aside from the minor hiccups mentioned earlier though - there's decks that work well together such as Visionary and Haka, where Visionary causes Haka to draw loads of cards and Haka consumes them all in his power up moves, and Absolute Zero works beautifully on his own to back up most any roster of teams. Villains will often require you to act a certain way to counter them, or generally favour a certain type of team, but it's pretty fun to learn these and beat them once you've figured out the patterns.
I'd give it a decent 8/10!

There's a lot to like about this game. For a third-person shooter, the setting (a post-catastrophe Dubai) was definitely a  departure from the norm and the devs did a great job in balancing the tone of the game with a vibrant colour palette. Similarly, the devs attempted to deliver a game that depicts a more realistic, gritty version of modern war that requires the player to make a number of morally difficult decisions and for the most part I felt they achieved this. What starts off as a bit of a bland story becomes increasingly engrossing, departing from the standard fare of most shooters. Unfortunately, the game is slightly held back from greatness by its run of the mill gameplay, incorporating mainly wave after wave of shooting galleries and a relatively poor cover system. All in all, while by no means a complete package, the game delivers a unique perspective on war that merits giving it a try when on sale.

I've played this game on multiple platforms, so don't let my short play time guide you.
It's not a game to kick back and relax with. It's not a game that will make you feel like a hero or a champion. It is a game that challenges the player to look at their world a little differently. It takes a while for it's true colors to shine through, but the story it tells and how you react to it can tell you a lot about yourself.

In Spec Ops: The Line you are given the role of Captain Generic Tough Guy and given a simple mission to go to Dubai and rescue/kill Colonel Kurtz from
. To the shock of everyone who has never played a video game, seen a movie, read a book, or experienced any sort of narrative in any context, things go to♥♥♥♥♥♥
Your expectations are set up for this to be a standard forgettable modern 4-hour single player third person shooter experience - corridors leading into shooting galleries with waist-high cover leading into another corridor leading into epic cutscene. Repeat until done. From a gameplay perspective Spec Ops follows this unerringly, and while the gunplay is satisfactory it's purely a vehicle to advance the story.
As any review will tell you, the only reason anyone played or remembers this game is that story, which I was looking forward to. I expected some 'moral choices' in the vein of games like
, where you have to stop a train from running into a bus of schoolchildren by rerouting it to a puppy farm. That sort of thing.
The reality is even less interesting and more two-dimensional than that. About halfway through the game you are forced to
completely unintentionally and without the option to not do so. I went around and checked. There's no other way to progress the story.
Afterwards, the shocking reveal that
is supposed to really trigger a guilt response, but I can't feel guilty about something I literally had no choice in. Not even "hey man, it was him or me" kind of choice, it's a "if you want to play Spec Ops, you're going to do this".
Anyway. It wasn't any worse than any of the hundreds of murders of random NPCs I had just killed to get to that point, or the hundreds more I would kill on my way to the next cutscene. And it's hard to weep about the above when every 10 seconds you get video game-y bullet time effects and gratuitous explosions of heads from headshots from a simple pistol shot.
Futher undercutting any sort of emotional resonance this game is going for is the weird sense of humor of Colonel Kurtz, who is only slightly less over-the-top than Handsome Jack from
. You get quips like "aw, you shot that guy? he was my favorite!" in your radio as you mow down dozens of identical baddies.
All that together makes for a very schizophrenic experience - Spec Ops wants to have its Games Are Art™ cake and eat it too, and fails on both ends.
Spec Ops: The Line has mediocre gameplay and an emotionally exploitive story that is designed to make you feel bad, but doesn't go far enough and doesn't even look at itself before pointing a finger at you. If you want to be manipulated or have your emotional rug pulled out from other you, there are other games that do it far better and are more fun, too. Give this a hard pass.

Many people say Divine Divinity is a clone of Diablo having in regard the implemented combat system. Well, they're right. But except that the game derives many features from classic cRPG games which makes it far more complex than enjoyable, but still very primitive in gameplay Diablo (1&2).
If You really want compare Divine Divinity to other well known games to have some reference, then I must say this game is an offspring of Diablo 2 and Baldurs Gate 2. It inherits the combat system from Hack&Slash, which makes fighting very fleshy and satisfying. Other characteristic features are random loot placement, limited class selection (warrior, mage and rouge) and no companions.
The story telling  on the other hand is a classic cRPG. Destiny places our protagonist in the wrong place in the wrong time, entangling him/her in fight for sirvival, initially for his/hers own life, but eventually for the sake of whole world. And the world is really BIG in this game. You will visit villiges, big cities, wander forests and impenetrable darknses of dungeons. In that time You will meet many interesting NPCs which You can speak, trade and fight, accomplish about 80 side quests not necessarily involving fighting, and even solve puzzles, some involving the physic engine implemented in the game! Did I told the player can even make a camp or decorate his/hers home? No problem with that in Divine Divinity.
I could write a whole article about this game, but instead I encourage to play it on Your own. The best two recomendations I can give are that Divine Divinity was listed among the "Top 100 PC Games Of All Time" by PC GAMER in 2012. The second one is telling You to listen to the game soundtrack composed by Kirill Pokrovsky, especially the "Drunk with dwarven mirth".
Have a nice game ;)

If you're a fan of classic isometric (Baldur's Gate, Fallout) RPGs, you'll at least have a huge appreciation for Divine Divinity.
Divine Divinity has more of a feel to it like Ultima VII does, and is unfortunately an often overlooked game of the genre:
It feels epic, has an interesting storyline and it has a fun, open world.
One of the things I like most about the game is that enemies don't respawn and once you've cleared the map, you've cleared it for good, making it feel like you've actually progressed unlike games such as the Diablo series, so if you're looking to become overpowered or overleveled, this isn't the game for you as it can be challenging at times.
Overall, one of the best CRPGs out there, and definitely worth a look especially for the price of it here on Steam.

First off I have to mention that this game is incredibly buggy or at least the Steam version is, since it's apparently lacking a major patch. There are a ton of quests that don't work at all or are partially broken. Some people even said that they can't finish the game because of some major bugs. Also, avoid exploring an area before you have a quest that requires you to go there, MANY quests can be broken by doing stuff before you're asked to.
I've played this game many years before but I returned to it now after about 10 years.
Combat: You click on enemies once and you also have to spam potions. Spamming potions is mandatory since the developers found it very fun and innovative to not give you health OR mana regen. This doesn't add anything to the game, it only makes it tedious. You only have to spend a few hundred gold coins on mana potions and then you can spam spam spam. Basically, thanks to the game trying to be "tactical" and♥♥♥♥♥♥by forcing you to use potions, you have infinite health and mana.
Actually it ain't. There are 2-3 spells that are worth your time and they look like crap. Also, you're going to have to rely on melee/ranged a lot since you don't want to waste mana on the easy mobs.
The starting spell of the mage called "meteor strike" is a yellow football followed by an ugly looking smoke effect. That's what you're gonna have to use for the first 20-30 levels because most of the other spells are pathetic. The spells aren't satisfying to use AT ALL, it's depressing. The effects are boring to look at, they lack power, and the sound effects don't make you feel like you're actually a powerful mage. You can also cheese the game with Freeze and frost weapons.
The quests are actually the best part of the game, they're rarely fetch quests or "kill 10 sewer rats" quests but even after you've done them all you feel like you had little impact on the world besides getting special responses from unnamed NPCs based on your reputation level. The reputation system, however, is broken, some quests give you +0 rep and some substract reputation when they shouldn't (you saved that ♥♥♥♥♥ from the zombie? -4 rep for you). Again, more and more bugs.
The music is great as well, it makes the game atmospheric, too bad the game itself is lacking in substance.
The storyline is simple and boring, you have to kill a cult that wants to destroy the world. The dialogue is so bad it's as if it was written by a 12 year old, they try too hard to make it sound funny and most of the time it's not. The animations are bugged when you play it on a modern system, most animations are running at very high speed and look odd.
Only play this game if you just want to waste time playing an isometric RPG just for the sake of doing it. It's literally a big pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥ it even has the bugs. It's not even a good Diablo clone, there are better clones out there, like the Sacred series, Titan Quest, Torchlight, Path of Exile, etc. Some people compared this game to the Ultima series so try out those games instead of  torturing yourself with this crap.

Call of Duty Black Ops 2 Multiplayer Review (9/10):
The multiplayer is really improved in this CoD.Treyarch succesfully improves the MP with the new Pick-10 system.The hook of Pick 10 comes from the ability to defy the loadout rules. Each attachment, weapon, grenade or perk counts as one of your ten points, and you can swap them out at will to create a huge number of combinations. Treyarch has also added in Wild Cards, which allow you to spend additional points to break even more rules, like equipping two primary weapons or up to six perks. Multiplayer maps like Hijacked or Nuketown 2025 are all about madness and fun!

Okay so I'm a Call of Duty fan and absolutely love the FPS genre. Call of Duty: Black Ops II is one of my favorites in the COD franchise, Black Ops I being my favorite, and I believe that any COD fan should play this game. Although, this games does have its downsides.
Flaws:
-Mouse Acceleration that I cannot turn off
-Constant crashing when loading up the game
Those two flaws are huge ones for me because I absolutely HATE mouse acceleration and if the game won't launch, I can't even play it!
Also this game is old. It really isn't that big of a deal but, very few people play online. I was on last night and only 600 people were playing it.
The campaign of this game I can't say is my favorite but I did enjoy it. The campaign was also very innovative. This game has multiple endings depending on your choices and there are some optional missions that I think are worth playing.
Multiplayer in this game is arguably one of the best in all of Call of Duty..... or used to be. As I stated earlier there are very few people online and the mouse acceleration assists in making me struggle to get even one kill. I do although love the guns accessible and the Pick-10 Create a Class system is my favorite from the franchise. This multiplayer at its peak was and is still my favorite.
Like I said, I'm a huge fan of the FPS genre and I absolutely love any game I can get my hands on. I am a HUGE fan of COD Zombies. Started since World at War and still going on strong. The zombies in blops 2 had some of the best maps, and some of the worst. The map Tranzit is the first map you can play (that contains an easter egg). This is one of the worst maps imo. I hate the buildable wonder weapon called the Jet Gun. Once you build it, the weapon is a cool-down type weapon to where you can use it until it over heats. But it flat out sucks and if the gun overheats, IT BREAKS. All the pieces fall apart and you HAVE TO REBUILD IT. "Jet Gun 2/10 only good for the memes" -IGN.
Then we get to the good maps later on like Mob of the Dead, Buried, and Origins. Granted these 3 are the only DLC maps (not including Nuketown Zombies). I love all of these maps because to me they were fantastic! I can't put that any other way unless I extend it another 1,000 Words. Zombies was also innovative introducing many new wonder weapons and BUILDABLES. One of the best things to touch zombies. The AI was fine by me and the weapons in zombies were pretty so-so. Zombies in this game 9/10, 2nd best zombies.
-TL;DR
Black Ops II is an amazing innovative and extremely fun game. If you wanted to buy the game, buy it on a console if you can. If not, do not pay full price for the game. Wait until a sale or buy the steam activation code from a different website ex.♥♥♥♥♥ I reccomend this game, but not on this platform.

The best of the GTA series, and perhaps one of the greatest games I have ever played. There are no words to describe this game. Yes, the graphics are a bit dated, but that's what ENBs were created for. What matters is the gameplay, story, voice-acting, and just the scope of the world. They run the gamut of ecosystems, from cities and towns to farms, mountains, forests, rivers, and deserts. All of the cities feel plausible, and there's a crapton of stuff to do, from shooting pool at the bar and getting a bite to eat at the local pizza joint, to hijacking cars, running from police, gunning down rival gang members, and best of all, MASS GENOCIDE.
There are a few Hollywood celebrities in the game's voice-cast, including Samuel L. Jackson as a crooked cop (who is the main antagonist), Peter Fonda as a hippie, James Woods as a government agent, Wil Wheaton as a news reporter on the radio, and Andy♥♥♥♥♥♥as a radio talk-show host who is a bit too passionate about gardening.
The game's setting is definitely influenced by Boyz N The Hood, but later goes into the mafia influences of previous and later games. All of the vehicles have their own unique character, and I'm not lying when I say you can drive ANYTHING, from cars, trucks, and buses to trains and boats to planes and helicopters (including the ultimate weapon for any homicidal maniac, a VTOL jet fighter). You can even get around using a stolen jet pack!
The weapons in the game cover a wide variety, from knives, baseball bats, shovels, and katanas, to pistols and shotguns, to machine pistols and assault rifles, and even rocket launchers, flamethrowers, chainsaws, and miniguns. Hint: go to the busiest highway you can find and open fire with the heavy weapons.
If you do not buy this game, you will not be living AT ALL. GTA V may be the newest and have all the bells and whistles, but we would be remiss if we forgot the origins of Los Santos. And besides, neither of my computers can play GTA V. For the lower-end people, GTA: SA is the way to go. Not too graphically-demanding, and packed full of hours of entertainment and story.
Above all else, though, remember to FOLLOW THE DAMN TRAIN.

What can I say about this game? One of my first GTA... and one of my favorites. I will always love this game. Great story and a very large world (in 2005 it was cool) and a lot of opportunities and freedom of action. Lots of interesting (and not) missions, as well as many other interesting places. I could continue to describe this game... but better to play it and rate it. Thank you RockStar for this wonderful game.

TLDR: What a pile of poo! I understand some people feel some nostalgia re-playing this game but for whoever has played more recent games, unless you love the GTA franchise and want to know more about it, just ignore this game.
2004 is quite far away but man does this game feel dated and does it smell of console port all over the place.
Don't get me wrong, the game is playable but controls are clunky and poorly explained (sometimes leading to mission failures and forcing you to search online for help). The first sign of bad port came from the default keybinding. I always have a first look at keybindings before jumping into a game and remap a few things here and there. In GTA SA, I ended up spending 15min in the start menu remaping MOST controls since it was completely off! I've never seen such a poor choice of default keybindings. On the good side, most keys have only one action attached to it.
The interface feels sluggish (map can't be access with the press of a button, switch between crouching and standing only happens when you stand still...).
The game has some boring gameplay mechanics inherited from a lost era: you remember those sport games where you had to smash buttons as fast as possible to win a pathetic race... yeap, GTA SA's got that too because that was fun! Oh, the fond memories... Want to go faster on that push bike of yours, please tap the forward button like a mad man. Oh, and make sure to control the steering at the same time. You'll be in for a treat!
You don't seem to be able to carry any kind of health boost item and health kits seem pretty seldom on the map meaning you'd better be careful during missions.
And if you fail a mission, you have to drive back to where you got the mission in the first place (from wherever you failed the mission or the hospital if you died) and start over again. Thankfully the game allows you to skip some parts... sometimes. For some reason some driving parts can be skipped but not others, and some videos can be skipped but not others... It's just a mess.
I liked the idea of leveling skills and having some kind of fitness management. I was looking forward for the neighbourhoods fights and taking over the city since I enjoyed this in other more recent games. I was ready to put my disdain for the modern ghetto gangsta theme aside and focus on the gameplay but the gameplay is simply not fun enough.
This game, in its current state and in the current market is only for 3 kind of people:
_ gamers who enjoyed it when it came out and like the nostalgia trip
_ fan of the GTA franchise who want to learn more about it
_ people who exhausted their entire game library and have nothing else better to do with their lifes

Review:
I was not a fan that they released this game in chapters which was pretty much 1 story mission each but didnt really matter since I just bought the collection of chapters in one bundle. Story wise it was interesting and as a fan of the series I could tell this was more of a Origins type game. Gameplay feels improved compared to the older games, but the system to unlock new gear/weapons really feel short for me. They expected you to replay the same few missions over and over again to unlock things. As far as a recommendation, its worth it if you want to follow the story which will be important for any sequels, or if you like mindless repetition of being an assassin, which I get bored of quickly.

I wasn't always a particular fan of the Hitman franchise, sure it was fun, but I always thought the games were 'good', not 'great'.
Then I heard about this Hitman. I was somewhat excited. Then I heard it would be episodic. Away my excitement was.
But actually the fact that this game was in episodic form may have actually helped it. You see, normally you would play a level and progress to the next. However in this hitman game there is great benefit from replaying a level and playing in different styles/goals etc. This showed me how detailed the levels actually were and made me appreciate it much more.
The gameplay is great and gives room for various playstyles, the fact that people can create their own 'missions' really adds to the replay-ability too. Graphically this game is amazing aswell, it can be demanding, but boy does it look nice.
Apart from that, the UI is good, the introduction videos are super cool and the soundtrack isn't much special but hey, it's not half bad.
You can try the first mission for yourself, if you like it, buy the first season, totally worth it!

The game plays pretty much like Half-Life 2 but the difficulty is ramped up with stronger enemies which you gotta put down hard. There are also way more of them. I found myself getting surrounded if I moved forward too quickly. The game has some challenging puzzles that you'll have to think outside the Half-Life box to progress. The game looks great and the music really builds on the atmosphere the developers created. One thing that really makes this game stand out is the level design. Very good use of the environments which feel more like the original Half-Life.
I highly recommend giving this one a go if you are a Half-Life fan.
Even if you haven't played through the half-life series I would still recommend this game.

Sentinels of the Multiverse is a super hero themed single player/cooperative card game that offers a unique twist on the genre by having you manage a team of heroes with unique abilities instead of playing units to fight your opponent. Unlike most card games, all cards are available from the start--you don't have to unlock anything. There is a physical version of the game, and this digital version is perfectly accurate to the physical one.
People familiar with card games similar to Magic will find some very basic similarities in this game, but for the most part, Sentinels is fairly unique. Rather than pitting you against another player, you (and up to 4 other people) choose 3 to 5 hero decks and are tasked with playing against a villain deck that runs itself while dealing with the hazards posed by an environment deck. Unlike Magic and its derivatives, instead of fighting with creatures or units, your team of heroes relies entirely on their innate abilities and the various passive, active, and one-shot abilities represented by their cards to defeat their opponents.
Sentinels offers a fresh, interesting take on the card game genre and pulls it off very well. Every villain poses a fun, unique challenge and every hero has its own, interesting way of taking on those challenges and synergizing with other heroes. Even the locales in which you play bring their own unique flavor to the game and shake up the way you approach your goal. Sentinels is a lot more about the rules set by each specific villain and location than it is about its basic rules, which means gameplay varies more than in other card games from match to match.
Its cooperative gameplay also sets Sentinels apart from other card games, and makes it one of the few options out there for people who like card games but aren't interested in a competitive experience.
Though the art on some of the older cards may be a bit simplistic, which actually made me overlook the game at first, the art on newer cards has improved a lot. Overall, Sentinels has a very charming art style appropriate to its comic book theme.
With so many combinations of heroes, villains, and evironments--along with advanced difficulty mode and monthly challenges published by the developers--Sentinels offers a LOT of replayability.
Simply put, Sentinels is a lot of fun to play. For TCG/CCG veterans, it's a unique, refreshing take on a familiar and somewhat stagnant genre; for players new to the genre, it's an accessible card game that's fun and easy to learn yet offers plenty of depth to hold their interest. The art may not be as breathtaking as what you'd find on most popular card games, but
.

+High replay value
+Nice soundtrack

If you're not familiar with the physical card game, I'd recommend trying the free demo to get a taste.  This review is for people who've played the physical version and are curious about the digital.
While there are card games I'd never play on the PC, this one takes all problems of tracking modifiers and keeping up with all the cards, and automates it for you.  No longer will you have to worry about keeping up with... say... a game involving the Matriarch (and all her birds!) versus Unity (and all her mechanical golems), Ra (and his fire modifiers for everyone), Wraith (and her stacking damage reduction), Tachyon (and counting the burst cards in her deck), in a battle in Dry Gulch (and all those freaking modifiers!), while shuffling decks as you look for assorted key cards on a rapidly shrinking table space.
Seriously, this game takes all that and makes it -easy- and -fun- again.
It also means I'll probably be dumping my physical cards soon, since I don't think I can ever go back to playing it by hand again.  (A shame, since I have a large set of Cauldron cards all printed out)

Overall, a really solid and enjoyable game; great world, great story, and lots and lots of quests, secrets, and odds and ends to explore, basically everything that makes an amazing classic RPG. That being said, if you don't like the elements of a classic RPG (slower pace, character building, lots of text, running around and, of course, older graphics), this probably isn't your game, but if you do, get this game right now.
I do have two warnings though. First, the magic system is subpar, or at least the combat spells are. They do little damage, but don't cost too much and cast as quick as you click, so as a mage you just end up spamming your right mouse button until things fall over... consider fighter instead.
Second, the game has a few ridiculously hard bosses. I never actually managed to finish the game as the second-last boss was immune to all my spells, could always blind me (I think it bypasses all resistances), and could insta-kill me and all my maxed-out summoned minions. Getting to a high enough level isn't enough, you pretty much have to be following a guide to stand a chance of finishing, and being forced to min/max really spoils the experience for me.
Still, those are the only things I found wrong. Even at full price, you really can't go wrong with such a gem; just stick with it through the first quest (it'll feel like a bit of a slog at first), make sure you are following some form of guidance for leveling, and you're in for a great time.

It was late, just past midnight. After hours of skulking around in the farmer’s field I had found my target, an orc who had carelessly wandered away from his fellow bandits and their camp. I stayed low and crept close behind him. Distracted by the farmer’s dog he didn’t stand a chance, I pounced. The blade of my dagger slid across his fat green throat and he squealed like a stuck pig. I couldn’t help but smirk at the carelessness of this buffoon as I looted his overfed corpse, another victim to my insatiable desire for blood and gold. I wasn’t able to admire my handiwork for very long though, just then the brush began to rustle up ahead prompting me to make my escape. Barely avoiding a confrontation with his friends who had heard his scream, I watched them howl in anger and grief as they suck out whoever had slayed their friend. But alas I had eluded them. I snaked my way into the farmer’s barn where I laid low and made my bed in the hay. While lying in the hay I could hear the snorts and howls of the orcs echo in the distance, their sorrow would soon be quelled because tomorrow night it would be their turn…

What is Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition?
The Definitive editon offers a brand new area with two new skills, it did some minor changes and overall polishing so basically it's just an upgrade from the normal version.
What is Ori?
Ori can with few words be described as a 2D platformer, but it's not just that. Ori and the Blind Forest is an amazing game with stunning graphics and beautiful music.
The first ten minutes of the game (prolog) tells the soul-crushing story of Ori and Naru. Naru saves Ori and takes care of him/her. Towards the end (of the prolog) Naru dies, and Ori sets out on an adventure. In the matter of these few minutes we fall in love with the two characters and this is something not many games can do.
The game has a bunch of abilities that you unlock throughout the game and these help you progress, and open new areas/paths and secrets in previous areas. In most games backtracking is boring but that is not the case here. However this largeg amount of abilities can be quite overwhelming and it is easy to lose track of them all and therefore get stuck in certain parts of the game.
Ori offers plenty of modes to play, easy, normal, hard, and no-death mode. This gives replay value to the game and makes you come back to it when you have finished it.
And thus i end up giving Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition a
95/100.

In any case, I highly-recommend this game.

Are you having an obsolete or low spec PC? Are you looking for some good game for some small money? Are you an open world games fan? Are you an oldschool gamer?
This is the game for you!
GTA San Andreas - My first GTA Game i played for real and, a game I probably don't need to introduce to anyone, unless they either spent last 15 years in a cave, or with no computer, or simply were doing time in slammer for murder. A Game that probably anyone who calls himself a gamer knows.
This is game that really got me into games like this. I was around 8 years old when i played it for the first time (I'm 17 as I write this review),
And I instantly loved that game. This game is 10 euros but gives as much or more fun as those expensive new titles.
Now to the real deal.
-Graphics? Probably best you could get in 2005.
-Gameplay? Fascinating, amazing and immersive.
-Character customization? You name it you got it - Tattoos, haircuts, Clothes, martial arts, and, what's impressive for such an old game, Fat and muscle levels which actually affect protagonist's body in pretty much real time.
-Story? Dear authors...y u no hollywood yet?
-Easter eggs? Of course! Pretty good ones, it's a rockstar's game afterall.
-Bugs? yep, they happen, however nothing really disturbing unless it happens excessively (which appears to happen rarely).
-Modding? Sure thing. There are tons of good mods, scripts, models, textures etc. You'll just need to downgrade the game since usual steam version can't be modded.
-Map? Pretty big and well detailed with lots of interesting places.
-Soundtrack? Really good, eventhough I mostly listen to rap, I enjoy listening to almost any radio station in the game.
-Worth the price? How do you even dare to ask? Absolutely yes!
In short - Get this game. You won't regret it. Total 10/10.
Any questions? Let me know in the comments.
Thank you for reading.

The tabletop version of Sentinels of the Multiverse is a cooperative puzzle/risk-management game in which each player takes the role of a single Hero with a customized deck. The players then work together to cover each others' weaknesses and bring down the Villain. A third type of deck, Environment, defines the place the fight is taking place and adds complications.
In the video game version, a single player takes control of the entire heroic team, unless you're using online multiplayer. Bizarrely, it's actually easier this way; the single player has more to keep track of, but can manage all the heroes as a unit. It makes it MUCH easier to pull shenanigans, like making sure multiple heroes keep their pieces of a card combo ready for use or having one entire hero present for the sole purpose of dying (poor Tempest ...)
Overall this is a fun card battler, with a lot of potential for growth. It should be noted, though, that it's seriously on the easy side for a cooperative game. While something like five out of six games of Knizia's Lord of the Rings or two out of three games of Elder Sign end in failure, I've only ever lost against Sentinels of the Multiverse when playing carelessly or going for a "stunt" victory for an achievement. Using three-hero teams and avoiding using more than one of the most powerful heroes (Legacy, Tachyon, Visionary) will help to mitigate this.
Note: Yes, this game divides its characters among a LOT of different DLC packs. Note, though, that these just exist to parallel the expansions the base game has received, and $5 for a DLC expansion vs. $30+ for the same expansion in cardboard isn't too bad.

An aging gem of a mod.
Level and skirmish design is where this mod truly shines. Many instances of clever design overshadow many of the game's shortcomings.
This may be an unpopular opinion, but I never thought that the weapons in HL2 were all that great, especially the ones that transfer over into MINERVA. The SMG lacks kick. The pistol is a pea-shooter. The revolver is kind of nice and so is the shotgun, but revolver ammo is scarce and about half the game is played without the shotgun.
Having grenades and melee weapons as holdable weapons is just poor design. These should be instant activation buttons, not items you switch to, then activate.
The story is a bit on the pretentious side. It's delivered mostly through text, but still manages to be decent enough. It's set in the world of Half Life around the time of HL2, it seems. It's a side story that meshes well with the existing story.
The way the pacing ramps up toward the end is stellar. There are some truly great skirmishes happening at the end.
I recommend giving this one a play. Great level design and skirmishes never truly get old, even if many other things do.

I would argue that this is Treyarch's best game. The gameplay is still that classic fast paced, action packed, movie-like atmosphere only they added something new to the Call of Duty series. They added decision making. You can alter the story as you move along based on your decisions and end up with different endings.
The story is fun and the main villain is very well done. The voice acting is really good as well but that isn't really anything new to the Call of Duty series at the time this one was released.
Technically, this is a spiritual successor to the original Black Ops in that some of the characters are back but overall you wouldn't really need to play the first game to understand this one. This is a cool story all on its own.
The number one feature that this one has though is the ability to choose your layout before the mission starts. If I recall, this was the first in the Call of Duty series to feature this and it is a great feature to have.
All in all, great game.

"Super Meat Boy...Super Mario Bros...coincidence?" 10/10
Have you ever picked up a video game and instantly fell in love with it? I have, and growing up in the early 90's with popular consoles like the 'Super Nintendo' and the 'Sega Genesis' have given many platformers extremely nostalgic feelings for me. Then I got older and video games changed just as much as I did and when I came back to them many years later I found that they had turned into something that I didn't understand, appreciate, or recognize. Every game seemed to blend in with the ones around it, and I wasn't all that happy with the majority of games that I was playing. This is the game that changed that.
'Super Meat Boy' is easily one of the best games that I have ever played and rivals some of the greatest platformers of all time like 'Mario Bros', 'Castlevania', 'Mega Man', and so on and so forth. This game put 2D platforming, along with indie gaming back on the map for many people because everything about it is simply amazing. From the soundtrack, to the controls, to the level design, to the insanity of it all; 'Super Meat Boy' will keep you addicted until the very end. And just when you think you've mastered it all, you discover there are even harder versions of each and every level that you've already played. If you are at all into side-scrollers this is a must buy. Hell, this is a must buy even if you aren't.

Let me get my one negative out of the way first. This game has little to no story. I have to be honest. The way the story is told in this game is through these very brief cutscenes after the mission as well as your instructor giving you a small background on the target before the mission. Because of the way the story is told it's very hard to not only follow the story but to introduce and develop characters.  The story of hitman has to do with this organization, called providence. It's made up of the most powerful people in the world, weather there known the the public or not.
Moving past the story i want to talk about the stellar gameplay and the new systems put in place after Absolution. The gameplay is great it really is. Few game can get my heart pounding out of my chest while im doing the tutorial level for the 4th time. Yes i did the tutorial level 4 diffrent time because i wanted to 100% it. 100%-ing each level is something i want to do but i just don’t know if i have time, these levels are massive and ot took me 2 hours to 100% the tutorial, which is on a medium size yacht. The point is that these levels are enormous and seemingly endless. And that makes for an open world experience in a closed environment. I actually kind of do want to elaborate on that. I cannot recall a game where a developer has done this.
Aside from open areas in a linear storyline, but this game feels like is a huge world to explore partially because the levels are so big. And i say partially because they are huge and ill eloborate on that in a minute but the othr reason they feel open world is because there is so much diversity in not only settings but people and surroundings as well, I think the best level to example this is “Colorado” Where your tasked with killing 4 people of different backrounds.  I want to highlight how close the orchord and the house are together. They are a few steps away but they are drastiaclly diffrent. On the orchard you’ll find appricotts while in the house you’ll find huge coputer towers and stuff. They are super diverse and it's a huge change in scenery which i absolutely love.
System wise everyone knows about the opportunity system implemented in this new game and all i want to say is that it’s perfect. Each opportunity is different, each opportunity is different and each use their environments in different ways. There's one where you can make a guy have an OCD attack or there's one where you can dress up as a plague doctor. There's even one where you can dress up as a famous model. There awesome and best of all their creative. And that's what makes them special. No opportunity even echos a different one.
Let me Talk about level design for a minute and how perfect it is. Every game should try to have level design  as good as hitman’s. Every area has certain people allowed to be in and you can be that person by taking a disguise. So a cook cannot go up stairs but a military operative can. HOWEVER there's an added level of depth where if you were to take the same scenario of the military operative being allowed to go upstairs, maybe the operative can’t go into the kitchen. Hitman is designed like this, your disguise acts like a key card of some sorts but just because you have a different disguise on doesn't mean you can go to a certain part of the map. You can always sneak around but depending on the security in place you may be shot on site. An example of this is the fact that a gardener cannot go into the underground secret lab. ‘Ok thats cool but what does that have to do with level design?’ Well absolutely everything. The way you move through the level is based off this disguise system. And that's really, really cool because it makes you explore.
I want to talk really quickly about planning your assassinations, as you do a level more and more you will work towards mastery, as long as you do it differently of course but once you get to certain levels of mastery, you unlock starting areas, weapons, etc. and you can use these to your advantage.  This is a very good reward for replaying levels, make it more interesting don’t make the player fix the same problem with the same tools, give them an allen wrench instead of a screwdriver and see what they do! Anyway, I just kind of wanted to mention this real quick

So this review is recommended only for those who really enjoy Batman, and just want more of it.
This game wasn't the game that was marketed to me. I expected to play a game based around batman's earlier years where Batman survives a night of relentless attacks from the 8 assassins hired to kill him. This premise sounded great when I saw the trailers for the game and got really excited to see some of these fights. However, the story they gave out was not only a lie, but a waste of a good storyline.
Now let me explain. Of the 8 assassins hired to kill you, 2 of them are side quests(Lady Siva and Deadshot), that you don't even need to complete(one of which isn't even given to you but has to be found. So you could technically miss it completely).
-Killer Croc's fight is a rehash of the Bane's fight from Asylum, which takes place so early in the game it could still be considered the "tutorial level".
-The Electrocutioner fight is a one hit "haha" moment. Which if this were a movie would be fine but it's not it's a game. I paid to play not watch.
-Deathstroke, the most exciting one for me, was boiled down to a QTE. Again, it looked cool, but if I wanted to watch this I'd buy a movie.
-Bane, was the same Bane fights as every other Bane fight.
So that’s 6 of the 8 assassins wasted. For a game that lasts about 20-22 hours the first three I listed take place within the first 1-2 hours of play. With Deathstroke and Electrocutioner happening within 20mins of each other. The other two (Copperhead and Firefly) were the only ones that were somewhat unique
And that really sums up this game's major problem. There's nothing new here. Most of the game is rehashed stuff from the other games. Not adding anything new to separate it from the previous instalments. They rushed the game and it doesn't seem like they even tried to up the experience for the player. I only replayed this game for the sake of the storyline, which it too is subpar aside from the Joker's origin which is to short to be excited about.
Then there's the combat. Idk what WB missed but this game's combat isn't as intuitive as the other games. I replayed the first Bane fight about 15 times because the game randomly targets Bane for your attacks. I'd be in the middle of a beatdown and then it jumps me across the arena and attacks Bane. And after that fight it stays broken. 25-30% of attacks don't go in the direction you point it to go.
TLDR - This game is subpar, adding nothing new to make it stand out enough. Only reccomended for those who really enjoy Batman or just wanna know what happens.
All in all this is the worst Arkham game that was released. Even in comparison to Knight, cause with all the problems that game had, at least it was a great game.

What is Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition?
The Definitive editon offers a brand new area with two new skills, it did some minor changes and overall polishing so basically it's just an upgrade from the normal version.
What is Ori?
Ori can with few words be described as a 2D platformer, but it's not just that. Ori and the Blind Forest is an amazing game with stunning graphics and beautiful music.
The first ten minutes of the game (prolog) tells the soul-crushing story of Ori and Naru. Naru saves Ori and takes care of him/her. Towards the end (of the prolog) Naru dies, and Ori sets out on an adventure. In the matter of these few minutes we fall in love with the two characters and this is something not many games can do.
The game has a bunch of abilities that you unlock throughout the game and these help you progress, and open new areas/paths and secrets in previous areas. In most games backtracking is boring but that is not the case here. However this largeg amount of abilities can be quite overwhelming and it is easy to lose track of them all and therefore get stuck in certain parts of the game.
Ori offers plenty of modes to play, easy, normal, hard, and no-death mode. This gives replay value to the game and makes you come back to it when you have finished it.
And thus i end up giving Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition a
95/100.

The main difference is that in OatBF, the focus is more on dodging enemies than fighting against them. For example, the "boss fights" are all escape sequences.
In any case, I highly-recommend this game.

This is one of those kind of rare games that "I keep coming back", one of the key elements of this game is immersion, every level and its attention to detail is amazing, although the level design is most of times a straight line it never gets boring. I think the core of this game is just absorbing every element of the story of this psychology thriller, like a simple tour in a heavy gritty mind of a man. That funhouse level is a perfect example that illustrates this, we simple run through this crazy madhouse fictionally inspired by a fictional tvshow inside the game, these elements try to be realistic in a way that they affect the character and complement the complexity of that fictional Noir York City. I come back to this game not because of the shooting or bullet time but because of the nightmarish feel it always leave me, the characters we interact with always seem crazy, strange and distant. Technically the physics were pretty good for it's time and the game was released with tools from the developer, something rare nowadays, so there are plenty of mods out there even total conversions. Call of duty black ops 2 is a great game, one of my favourate cods. obviously there are not as many players as the game is a few years old and some of the game modes are dead/hardly used. but the campaign, zombies and multiplayer [when you can find a game] provides endless fun.

Black Ops 2 was the top of the competitive scene back in its time, people would say it had the best competitive Multiplayer and a complex campaign with multiple choices that changed how your storyline would play out but the years have diluted the appeal somewhat and it’s not what it used to be for the average player. I'll break this review down to each different element the game has to offer so you can see if it’s worth your time and money.
The campaign continues where Black Ops 1 left off. It takes place in both the past and the future and jumps back and forth between the two every few levels so you get a taste of both Cold war era and future tech/ weapons. The campaign is pretty good in terms of the story but you can get lost very quickly with the amount of back and forth on the time lines but overall worth a play through if you enjoyed Black Ops 1.
Everyone who played Black Ops 2 back in the day loves this multiplayer. I recently played through to complete first prestige and while the guns and levels are good enough the only people left playing the game are either top level players with 100s of hours or a few noobie players like myself. There doesn't seem to be any in-between so you either end up doing really well or horribly. Most high level players use one overpowered SMG so you have basically no chance at close range or even medium range. This makes it really hard for new players to get into the game so I'd say pass on this one and stick to something like Black Ops 3 which has a more balanced player base and weapons.
The base game only includes 1 zombie map which on its own is a really fun and at the time of its release was a revolutionary map. The idea is you travel via a bus through a few small areas of differing theme (Garage, dinner, Farmhouse, Town). Aside from that it’s your typical zombie’s mode with weapons, perks & mystery box.
The kicker is there are 5 other zombie maps all locked behind DLC. Achievement wise this means with the base game you can only get 10/50 if that is something you are interested in. Then again this is quickly becoming a standard with all new call of duty games so I guess you can give it a pass there.

Pros:

Nice atmosphere

Cons:
Checkpoints seem to be a bit sparse, nothing major, but it is a bit annoying every now and then.
The AI at times is a bit odd, for example, if you're particularily fast at getting somewhere, soldiers who are supposed to be hunting you will run past you, firing potshots while desperately heading to the place where you entered the level. Also fast zombies ocasionally freeze or go into their default pose for a split second.
During some scripted events you can run behind you or forward and find freshly spawned soldiers standing about waiting for you to trigger their arrival, but they will quickly snap out of it and fire on you.
(I'm having a bit of a hard time finding other complaints, and even some of the ones I've listed feel nitpicky)
Overall, I'd highly recommend this for someone who's longing for a new Half Life game, or someone who's just looking for a fun little shooter. It feels professional, it's fun, and it has a great feel to it!

HITMAN 2016
Let me get this off my chest first.
The graphics are superb. The performance is alright but I get CTD's whenever a large amount of NPC's get alerted (Like a bomb going off in the middle of the PARIS fashion show and all the NPC's scatter, BAM CTD)
Now on to the rest of the review:
For starters, the game lets you approach your targets as you see fit.
That adds a lot of replay value to the game but I don't like how it can feel like a scavenger
hunt at times. This makes getting every challenge a chore but hey that's my opinion.
The level design for each episode is superb as there are multiple hiding spots and opportunities
to pull off a swift, clean or even gruesome kill. You can opt to follow the marked opportunities or make your own.
This varies as some levels have more to offer than others. The Paris level and the Hokkaido level are my favorites.
The Paris level's mansion is decorated superbly and the Hokkaido level is a really impressive sight. Plus the level specific Vampire and Ninja costumes are a blast to use.
They removed the ability to chain shoot, which to me is a welcomed change.
Despite this making people think that for all the training that 47 did, he should be able to take
on massive amounts of enemies at once. This is not the case, he is trained as an assassin and people will disagree as to whether or not that means he should be able to kill many people at once in a hail of bullets and not die.
Going back to why I like the fact that chain shooting is gone, would be that it punishes you for being sloppy. You can't press a button and just insta-kill all the guys in the room just so you don't compromise the mission.
The disguise system so far, I like. It does give you outfits that sometimes help you drive suspicions away from you but it doesn't make it so that no one can recognize that you aren't that new golf coach. There is always 1 NPC that can see through your disguise, so you are kept on your toes.
Mission variety gets mixed up when you play Escalation which gives you a series of instructions that escalate in difficulty. I do find that this HITMAN title is very accessable to people new to the franchise as the gameplay, while it can be difficult and it can punish you, it does not outright punish you.
You will learn and you will feel accomplished for having pulled off an unnoticed kill and to finish the mission.
Contracts Mode is my favorite as it is exactly like playing HORSE. Except you try to murder people the same way the contract maker did. Making your own contract is really fun as it encourages you to get creative and try to make an exceedingly difficult contract to stump fellow players.
Elusive targets are a nice option to play but you can only finish them once,
It feels like you're a real assassin taking contracts and it ups the immersion level for me.
I however dislike that to access most of the content like starting points and such, you need to always be online.
Square Enix, IO Interactive, please. I bought the game legally. I do not like being treated like I stole something I paid money for. So locking me out of the content I should be getting while I'm in offline mode is not cool at all.
I do hope for a season two if possible, more episodes, more weapons, more suits and content.
If you need a numerical rating, I suppose I give HITMAN 2016 an 8/10.

For example, a warrior swinging a two handed hammer while casting a freeze spell and throwing deadly scorpion traps is just one of many possible (and very effective) builds.
The limited voice acting and repetitive (sometimes uninspiring) music should be mentioned as the disadvantages of this classic rpg.

Alright, so it's time I wrote an actual review for this game.
How do I begin? I recieved this game through Humble Bundle and was quite excited to try it. From the first moment opening the game, I am flooded with many bright colors - not a bad thing in its own right. Immediately, it seems as though much of the artwork looks much worse up close than I had imagined. I can overlook artistic simplicity and the most basic of character design if the gameplay makes up for it. After all, nice artwork is really just a bonus in a really solid card game.
: it's a mess.
: after playing several games, let me say that the gameplay feels whelmingly complicated because you are in control of very little within the game. You will draw a lot of cards, you will discard a lot of cards. The cards you actually manage to play will slowly whittle down the villian's health. As the player, you manage 3-5 heroes that each has their own deck and trash pile, as well as a playing field. There is a predefined turn order starting with the villain, moving to your heroes, and ending with the environment. Your freshly baked cookie cutter heroes have enough variety to their cards at least, just enough to spend a stupid amount of time looking through awfully designed cards.
So gameplay is rather unbalanced, but these qualities do not make an awful game, just an underdeveloped one.
to this game is the DLC. There is several times the content of the game contained in the DLC. Copying the brilliant concept from the massive game failure Evolve, there will also be multiple DLC season passes. On top of that, the first season pass alone is twice the price of the game. So apparently, it was cheaper to build the entire game engine and starting content than some extra characters and environments.
is the UI. Oh god the UI. Someone needs to set these developers down in a room and explain what a readable text and stylized text are because they don't understand what either are. The player is constantly baraged with all sorts of difficult to read text that doesn't look suited to a comic book or easy to understand. The cards are a mess of difficult to read text that I often find myself reading multiple times to figure out what in the world I'm reading. Scaling of cards is another problem. Do to the nature of the text embedded on the cards, scaling them down looks horrendus. The UI also includes an order system that is brought up every time a group takes damage. This is fine when I need to select 2 of however many cards I want to deal damage to, but what about when there is only one, or when the whole group takes damage with no side effects? Cards also fly by giving just enough time to read them that it is frustrating when they suddenly disappear. On top of all this, the abbundance gradients and clashing colors don't exactly make me feel any better.
is the completely undelivered aspects of what it promises.
Sentinels of the Multiverse is a game with some potential. The comic book-esque style it advertised is horribly lacking. The UI is horrendous, the artwork is amatuer, and the music in not any better. If you can get past these flaws, all you have to look forward to is an unbalanced, shallow card game full of cookie cutter characters.
